Это изменение решает проблему, когда клиенты рассматривали все операции файловой системы как универсальные операции записи. Теперь они могут точно различать действия только для чтения и записи, идентифицировать идемпотентные операции и выделять потенциально деструктивные. Данное улучшение обеспечивает более точную работу пользовательского интерфейса и логики повторных попыток, значительно повышая удобство для клиентов и пользователей.
updates.source_content:
- # feat(filesystem): add ToolAnnotations hints to filesystem tools (#3045)

**Files touched**

- [src/filesystem/index.ts](../blob/HEAD/src/filesystem/index.ts) — add `annotations` metadata to each tool definition
- [src/filesystem/README.md](../blob/HEAD/src/filesystem/README.md) — document ToolAnnotations mapping for all filesystem tools

## Description

This change adds MCP `ToolAnnotations` (`readOnlyHint`, `idempotentHint`, `destructiveHint`) to all filesystem tools and documents the mapping in the filesystem README. MCP clients can now accurately distinguish read‑only vs. write tools, understand which operations are safe to retry, and highlight potentially destructive actions.

## Server Details

- **Server**: filesystem
- **Area**: tools (metadata returned via `listTools` / `ListToolsRequest`) and server docs

## Motivation and Context

Previously, the filesystem server did not expose ToolAnnotations, so many clients (e.g. ChatGPT Apps) conservatively treated filesystem tools as generic write operations. This led to:

- READ operations being surfaced with WRITE badges and confirmation prompts.
- No way for clients to know which write tools are idempotent or potentially destructive.

This PR aligns the implementation with `servers#2988` and updates the README to clearly document the semantics of each tool. Read‑only operations no longer need to be treated as writes, and destructive/idempotent behavior is explicit for UI and retry logic.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- `npm run build --workspace @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem`
- `npm test --workspaces --if-present`

## Breaking Changes

None.

* fix: use --frozen instead of --locked in release workflow

The release script bumps the version in pyproject.toml, which causes
the lockfile to be out of sync (uv includes the package's own version
in the lockfile). Using --frozen skips the lockfile freshness check
while still using pinned dependency versions.

- fix(everything): send elicitation directly from background task

Instead of waiting for the client to call tasks/result to trigger
elicitation, the server now sends elicitation/create directly from
the background process using sendRequest. This simplifies the flow:

- Server sends elicitation proactively when clarification is needed
- Client receives and handles it via existing elicitation handler
- Task resumes and completes after receiving the response
- Client's polling sees completed status

This approach avoids requiring the client to detect input_required
status and call tasks/result as a side-channel.

Fixes CI failures in PR #3220.

PR #3220 updated `mcp` library from 1.0.0 to 1.23.0, which caused test
failures due to a breaking change in `McpError` constructor API.

The `McpError` constructor now expects an `ErrorData` object instead of
a plain string message. This commit fixes the usage in `get_zoneinfo()`
function to use `ErrorData(code=INVALID_PARAMS, message=...)`.

```console
Error before fix:
  AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'message'
```

Also updates `mcp` dependency to >=1.23.0 in pyproject.toml to ensure
compatibility with the new API.

 ## Add project-context-mcp

  **Give Claude Code instant access to your project's institutional knowledge.**

  ### The Problem

  You're working with Claude Code on a complex project. Claude is smart, but it doesn't know your team's coding conventions, why you chose that architecture, or the gotchas in your codebase. You end up copy-pasting the same context into every conversation.

  ### The Solution

  Create a `.context/` folder. Drop in your docs. Now when you type `@` in Claude Code, your context files appear right alongside your source files:

  Help me add a new API endpoint @api-patterns.md @conventions.md

  One mention and Claude knows exactly how your team structures code.

  ### Features

  - **Zero config** - Just create `.context/` and go
  - **Selective inclusion** - Only include relevant docs per task (unlike CLAUDE.md which is always included)
  - **Supports everything** - Markdown, YAML, JSON, SQL, code examples, and more
  - **Smart naming** - Extracts titles from markdown headings for clean autocomplete

  ### Perfect for

  - Team coding conventions and standards
  - Architecture decision records
  - API design patterns
  - Database schemas and gotchas
  - Domain glossaries for complex industries

  ### Quick Start

  ```bash
  claude mcp add project-context -s user -- uvx project-context-mcp

  Links

  - GitHub: https://github.com/ericbrown/project-context-mcp
  - PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/project-context-mcp/

  ---
  Built for developers who are tired of repeating themselves.

updates.title: Updates in main (16 commits)
updates.summary_ru:
This update significantly enhances the CTTI data synchronization process, introducing continuous sync with total limits, incremental updates, and more robust error handling for batch failures. It also improves tokenization and chunking logic by correctly handling special tokens in `tiktoken` and adding accurate token recounting to `CodeChunker`, preventing OpenAI API errors. Furthermore, critical fixes ensure user cache invalidation occurs reliably upon changes to organization membership, eliminating stale data issues and 403 errors.

***

Этот релиз значительно улучшает процесс синхронизации данных CTTI, внедряя непрерывную синхронизацию с общими лимитами, инкрементальные обновления и более надежную обработку ошибок при пакетных сбоях. Также улучшена логика токенизации и разделения на чанки за счет корректной обработки специальных токенов в `tiktoken` и добавления точного пересчета токенов в `CodeChunker`, что предотвращает ошибки OpenAI API. Кроме того, критические исправления гарантируют надежную инвалидацию пользовательского кеша при изменении членства в организации, устраняя проблемы устаревших данных и ошибки 403.

Feat(CTTI): Continuous syncing with total limit

- Remove SyncFailureError when entire batch returns no results
- Return all None values instead, allowing entities to be skipped individually
- Only fail sync on true infrastructure errors (API key, auth, quota)
- Makes CTTI source more resilient to temporary unavailability

- Add cursor_class=CTTICursor and supports_continuous=True

- Create CTTICursor with last_nct_id and total_synced fields
- NCT_IDs are strictly increasing, ideal for cursor-based pagination
- total_synced tracks records synced across all runs to enforce limit
- Export CTTICursor in cursors __init__.py

- Merge pull request #1143 from airweave-ai/fix/revamp_ctti

Fix: Create WebEntities that scrape urls

- Merge pull request #1141 from airweave-ai/fix/tiktoken-special-token-handling

Fix: handle special tokens in tiktoken encoding to prevent sync failures

- Merge pull request #1142 from airweave-ai/fix/user-cache-invalidation-on-org-creation

Fix: invalidate user cache when organization membership changes

- Merge branch 'fix/user-cache-invalidation-on-org-creation' into fix/revamp_ctti

- Merge branch 'fix/tiktoken-special-token-handling' into fix/revamp_ctti

- fix: invalidate user cache after transaction commit, not before

Address review feedback: invalidating the cache before the transaction
commits creates a race condition where another request could repopulate
the cache with stale data (the old user_organization rows are still
visible to other transactions until commit).

Changes:
- _delete_user_organization_relationships now returns the list of affected
  user emails instead of invalidating the cache directly
- delete_organization_with_auth0 invalidates caches after the commit
- remove_member_from_organization already had correct ordering (after commit)
- create_organization_with_integrations already had correct ordering (after commit)

- fix: invalidate user cache when organization membership changes

When a user creates a new organization, the cached user data (which includes
user_organizations) was not being invalidated. This caused 403 errors when
the user tried to access the new organization because the cached user data
still only contained their previous organizations.

This fix adds cache invalidation in three places:
1. After creating a new organization
2. After removing a member from an organization
3. When deleting an organization (for all affected users)

This ensures that whenever a user's organization membership changes, their
cached data is invalidated so the next API request will fetch fresh data
with the updated user_organizations list.

- fix: handle special tokens in tiktoken encoding to prevent sync failures

When user content contains special tokens like <|endoftext|> (e.g., from
AI-generated text pasted into Linear issues), tiktoken.encode() raises a
ValueError by default. This caused sync jobs to fail completely.

Fixed by passing allowed_special="all" to all tiktoken.encode() calls,
which treats special tokens as regular text for token counting purposes.
This is correct behavior since we're only counting tokens for chunk size
management, not constructing model inputs.

Affected files:
- semantic.py: _recount_tokens_with_tiktoken()
- code.py: _recount_tokens_with_tiktoken()
- entity_pipeline.py: chunk statistics logging
- openai.py: token counting in embedder
- _base.py: count_tokens() in search providers

Fixes Linear sync failures caused by special tokens in issue content.

- fix: accept failed status in schedule execution test

The test validates that a schedule triggers a sync job, not that the sync
succeeds. Jobs may fail due to rate limits from other tests running in the
same CI pipeline, which is outside the scope of this test.

- Merge pull request #1140 from airweave-ai/fix/code-chunker-token-limit

fix(chunker): Add tiktoken recount step to CodeChunker to fix token limit bypass

- fix(chunker): Add tiktoken recount step to CodeChunker to fix token limit bypass

Root cause: Chonkie's CodeChunker reports incorrect (understated) token counts
because it counts tokens from individual AST nodes only, but the final chunk
text includes whitespace/gaps between nodes plus leading/trailing content.

This caused chunks with 9760+ actual tokens to slip through the 8192-token
safety net (which checked the incorrect Chonkie count), resulting in OpenAI
embedding API errors in production.

Fix: Add Stage 1.5 (_recount_tokens_with_tiktoken) between AST chunking and
the safety net, identical to how SemanticChunker already handles this.
The safety net now uses accurate tiktoken counts and correctly triggers
TokenChunker fallback for oversized chunks.

Fixes token limit exceeded errors for GitHub code file syncs (HTML templates).

- fix(ctti): tune hyperparameters for larger chunks + increase concurrency embedding

- SourceContext: source instance, cursor

- ScopeContextBuilder: builds ScopeContext
- InfraContextBuilder: builds InfraContext with logger dimensions
- SourceContextBuilder: handles source creation complexity
- DestinationsContextBuilder: creates destinations with native/custom handling
- TrackingContextBuilder: sets up EntityTracker, SyncStatePublisher

lacked discoverability, and required developers to know Docker commands
for common operations like restarting services or cleaning up volumes.

This rewrite adds self-documenting `--help` output, lifecycle
management flags (`--restart`, `--recreate`, `--destroy`), and styled
progress indicators that show wait counts during service health checks.

functions, making it easier to maintain and extend. Debug output is now
opt-in via `--verbose` rather than always-on, keeping normal runs clean.

Description from claude on the ignore

```
The issue is in next-env.d.ts at line 3, where there's a triple-slash reference directive (/// <reference types="..." />) that ESLint is flagging. This is actually a false positive because next-env.d.ts is an auto-generated file by Next.js, and triple-slash references are the correct way to include type definitions in this context.

To fix this, you should either:

Add the file to .eslintignore (recommended, since it's auto-generated)
Disable the rule for that specific file

updates.source_content:
- fix(svm): handle BigInt serialization in simulation error (#788)

* fix(svm): handle BigInt serialization in simulation error

Fixes #787

The SVM signer's simulateTransaction method uses JSON.stringify to
serialize error objects from Solana RPC responses. However, Solana
RPC often returns BigInt values (lamports, token amounts) in error
details, and JSON.stringify cannot serialize BigInt, throwing:
'Do not know how to serialize a BigInt'

This fix adds a replacer function to convert BigInt values to strings
before serialization.

* test(svm): add test for BigInt serialization in simulation errors

Adds a test case to verify that BigInt values in Solana RPC simulation
error responses are properly serialized to strings instead of causing
a JSON.stringify TypeError.

Одновременно было добавлено множество новых партнеров, таких как BlackSwan, Dexter и Rencom, а также фасилитатор AutoIncentive для сетей Base и Solana. updates.source_content:
- fix: skip dynamic bazaar import when extension is pre-registered (#982)

Add `hasExtension()` method to x402ResourceServer to check if an
extension is already registered. Update all HTTP middleware packages
(next, express, hono) to skip the dynamic import of @x402/extensions/bazaar
when the extension has been pre-registered.

This fixes deployment issues on serverless platforms (e.g., Vercel)
where dynamic imports with `webpackIgnore: true` fail because
node_modules are not available at runtime. Users can now pre-register
the bazaar extension using a static import:

```typescript
import { bazaarResourceServerExtension } from "@x402/extensions/bazaar"

const server = new x402ResourceServer(facilitator)
server.registerExtension(bazaarResourceServerExtension)
```

The static import is bundled correctly, and with this change the
middleware skips the dynamic import entirely, avoiding the runtime error.

- fix: filter synthetic confirm_changes tool results in ADK middleware

When using predictive state updates, the middleware emits a synthetic
`confirm_changes` tool call to trigger the frontend confirmation dialog.
However, ADK never actually called this tool, so when the frontend sends
back the tool result, ADK throws "No function call event found for
function responses ids" errors.

This fix:
- Filters out `confirm_changes` tool results in `_extract_tool_results`
  before passing them to ADK
- Tracks predictive state tool call IDs to suppress their TOOL_CALL_RESULT
  events (prevents frontend errors about missing function calls)
- Handles the case where all tool results are synthetic (confirm_changes)
  by marking them as processed and continuing with any trailing messages
- Enables follow-up requests after approving/rejecting changes

All 335 tests pass.

- fix(adk): skip consolidated text during streaming to prevent duplicates

When ADK streams text, it sends incremental deltas with partial=True,
followed by a consolidated message with partial=False containing the
complete text. Events with function calls have is_final_response=False,
so the existing duplicate detection was bypassed.

This fix uses ADK's explicit partial flag to identify consolidated
messages: if we were already streaming and receive partial=False,
skip the text content as it's a recap of what was already sent.

Fixes #742

Introduces a `defineAgents` helper function to ensure type safety when defining agent configurations.

This ensures that the integration ID matches one defined in `menu.ts` and that the agent keys are a subset of the features defined for that integration. This prevents runtime errors and improves code maintainability by providing compile-time validation of agent configurations.

With PROGRESSIVE_SSE_STREAMING enabled by default in google-adk >= 1.22.0,
ADK sends function call "previews" in partial events before the confirmed
call. This was causing duplicate TOOL_CALL_START events to be emitted.

confirmed calls (partial=False). Uses getattr with default False for
backwards compatibility with older google-adk versions.

Безопасность была улучшена путем добавления проверки UID клиента на XPC-сервере для предотвращения несанкционированного доступа к контейнеру после выполнения команды `su`, а сборки контейнеров теперь поддерживают встроенные Dockerfile через стандартный ввод. updates.source_content:
- Adds client uid validation to XPC server. (#896)

- When a user performs an `su` the effective UID changes but the bootstrap
  mach port does not, so that if container is running as `alice` from a
  GUI login session, it's possible to `su bob` and continue running
  container. While this doesn't pose a significant security risk as it's
  necessary for Alice to know Bob's password and manually enter it with
  `su`, this change closes the loophole by validating that client UID from
  the caller's audit token matches that of the API server.

- Fix container stats build break (#898)

Seems `run` was changed to return a data blob variant of stdout, which
made the function have a tuple of size 4 instead of 3 now. The stats
tests still used the old 3 wide variant which broke the build.

- Implement container stats (#851)

Closes #824

This implements statistics gathering across the various components, but
ultimately this is for implementing a new CLI command: `container
stats`. This shows memory usage, cpu usage, network and block i/o and
the number of processes in the container. The new command can inspect
stats for 1-N containers and by default continuously updates in a `top`
like stream.

## Motivation and Context
This PR implements the `container system df` command to display disk
usage statistics for images, containers, and volumes, along with their
total count, active count, size, and reclaimable space for each resource
type.

Active resources are determined by container mount references and
running state, while reclaimable space is calculated from inactive or
stopped resources.

Example output:
```
~/container ❯ container system df
TYPE           TOTAL  ACTIVE  SIZE      RECLAIMABLE
Images         4      3       4.42 GB   516.5 MB (11%)
Containers     4      2       2.69 GB   1.51 GB (56%)
Local Volumes  3      2       208.5 MB  66.2 MB (32%)
```

I'll have some follow-on PRs that will add `-v/--verbose` flag for
detailed per-resource information, `--filter` flag for filtering output
by resource type, and a `--debug` flag for debug statistics like block
usage, clone counts etc.

Ранее внутренний тип `Terminal` ошибочно инициализировался файловым дескриптором `stderr` вместо `stdin`, что мешало корректной работе с `stdout`. Теперь `Terminal` всегда инициализируется с `stdin` (дескриптор 0), а `stdout` и `stderr` получают свои правильные дескрипторы, что обеспечивает корректное перенаправление вывода.
updates.source_content:
- CLI: Fix -it not being able to pipe stdout (#951)

Fixes #949

Typically if one fd is a tty, it's common for all 3 of stdio to be the
same, but that is not always the case. In our case we were using our
Terminal type from Containerization to comb through err/out/in and give
us a type backed by one of the 3 if -t was supplied. It happens that
stderr is the first we check, so our Terminal() is backed by fd 2. This
change modifies things so that we always initialize our Terminal if
asked for with fd 0, and out/err are backed by their corresponding
correct fd number.

- Add Dependabot for GitHub Actions updates (#960)

## Summary

Add Dependabot configuration to automatically keep GitHub Actions up to
date.

## Changes

Adds `.github/dependabot.yml` configured to:
- Check for GitHub Actions updates weekly
- Group all action updates together for easier review
- Use `ci` prefix for commit messages

## Why

As discussed in #958, this helps:
- Keep actions up to date with security patches automatically
- Handle Node runtime deprecations proactively (e.g., Node 20 → Node 24)
- Reduce manual maintenance burden

## Reference

Based on the pattern used in
[swift-nio](https://github.com/apple/swift-nio/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml).

- Upgrade GitHub Actions for Node 24 compatibility (#958)

## Summary

Upgrade GitHub Actions to their latest versions to ensure compatibility
with Node 24, as Node 20 will reach end-of-life in April 2026.

## Changes

| Action | Old Version(s) | New Version | SHA |
|--------|---------------|-------------|-----|
| `actions/checkout` | v4 | v6 | `8e8c483` |
| `actions/download-artifact` | v4 | v7 | `37930b1` |
| `actions/upload-artifact` | v4 | v6 | `b7c566a` |
| `actions/labeler` | v5 | v6 | `634933e` |
| `actions/configure-pages` | v5 | v5 | `983d773` |
| `actions/upload-pages-artifact` | v3 | v3 | `56afc60` |
| `softprops/action-gh-release` | v2 | v2 | `a06a81a` |

## Context

Per [GitHub's
announcement](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-19-deprecation-of-node-20-on-github-actions-runners/),
Node 20 is being deprecated and runners will begin using Node 24 by
default starting March 4th, 2026.

### Why this matters

- **Node 20 EOL**: April 2026
- **Node 24 default**: March 4th, 2026
- **Action**: Update to latest action versions that support Node 24

### Security

All actions are now **pinned to commit SHAs** instead of mutable version
tags. This provides:
- Protection against tag hijacking attacks
- Immutable, reproducible builds
- Version comments for readability

### Automated Updates

A follow-up PR (#960) adds Dependabot configuration to automatically
keep these actions updated with new SHA-pinned versions.

### Testing

These changes only affect CI/CD workflow configurations and should not
impact application functionality. The workflows should be tested by
running them on a branch before merging.

Signed-off-by: Salman Muin Kayser Chishti <13schishti@gmail.com>

updates.source_content:
- Add support for reading env from named pipes (#974)

This is a fix for
[issue#956](https://github.com/apple/container/issues/956)

`FileManager.default.contents(atPath:)` returns `nil` for named pipes
(FIFOs)
and process substitutions like `/dev/fd/XX` because:
1. It expects regular files with a known size
2. Named pipes are stream-based and block until data arrives

## Solution
Use `FileHandle(forReadingFrom:)` instead, which:
- Properly handles blocking I/O
- Works with named pipes, process substitutions, and regular files
(mentioned in the
[doc](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/filehandle))

Co-authored-by: Bortniak Volodymyr <Bortnyak@users.noreply.github.com>

- Fix container auto-delete on rapid stop/start (#841)

Fixes #833.

Currently, when stopping and immediately restarting a container, it would fail with the error:
`“container expected to be in created state, got: shuttingDown”` and then be automatically deleted.
The `SandboxService` process waits five seconds before exiting after shutdown. During this interval, a rapid restart could reconnect to the still-terminating process in the `shuttingDown` state, triggering a state validation error.

This fix forcefully terminates the `SandboxService` process with `SIGKILL` upon container exit, instead of waiting five seconds. The bootstrap now defensively checks for and cleans up any stale services before registering new ones, preventing reconnections to processes in the `shuttingDown` state.

- ProgressBar: Various fixes (#1025)

There's a couple things I don't think are intuitive about this.

1. Because of the internal task, render() can still be called even after
finish() completes. Ideally async defers are supported and we could just
await the final render completing after cancelling the task and setting
.finished, but alas. To fix this we can just lock across the methods for
now.
2. We always clear the screen in the destructor, even if we don't use
the
progress bar. I don't think we should honestly do anything in the
destructor.
Feels a programmer error not to defer { bar.finish() } or call it
somewhere.
3. Our spaces based line clearing. Use the ansi escape sequence for
clearing line;
I think our calculations were slightly off and it would leave trailing
output ( "s]" )
in some cases.
4. Shrinking the window until the output is smaller than the terminal
window (and vice
versa) is wonky on various term emulators. Truthfully, this is just a
hard problem,
but we can truncate our output and still provide some useful info.

This fixes some single line output (cat /etc/hostname etc.) getting
cleared in our atexit handler, as well as the need for the usleep.

## Motivation and Context
Now that we're in 2026, we need to update the license headers on all the
files. Unfortunately, Hawkeye doesn't have an attribute for the current
year to help us avoid this in the future. Instead, I had to work around
this by doing the following:

1. Update licenserc.toml with:
     ```
      [properties]
       ... (other properties)
       currentYear = "2026"
     ```
 
2. Update scripts/license-header.txt with
    ```
Copyright ©{{ " " }}{%- set created = attrs.git_file_created_year or
attrs.disk_file_created_year -%}{%- set modified = props["currentYear"]
-%}{%- if created != modified -%} {{created}}-{{modified}}{%- else
-%}{{created}}{%- endif -%}{{ " " }}{{ props["copyrightOwner"] }}.
    ```

Then I removed these two changes before committing. After this PR is
merged, all files will have recently had git updates, so the existing
code for setting the modified year should work as intended.

- Fix port validation to allow same port for different protocols (#992) (#1000)

- Fixes: #992 
- Port validation previously rejected valid configurations
  when the same port number was used for different
  protocols (TCP and UDP). For example:
 `-p 1024:1024/udp -p 1024:1024/tcp`
  Although this is a valid and common use case, the
  validation logic treated it as a conflict.

To fix this, I updated the validation key to include the protocol name.
The validation now checks for overlapping port numbers only within the
same protocol, rather than across all protocols.

This change enables binding the same port number for both TCP and UDP,
aligning the validation behavior with real-world networking
requirements.

  containers.

  create command, after which the packets heading

This change adds --dns parameter support to the build command, matching
the existing functionality in the run command. This allows users to
specify custom DNS nameservers (like Google DNS 8.8.8.8) when building
container images, which is essential when the host machine uses a local
DNS resolver (e.g., 127.0.0.2) that doesn't work inside containers.

addresses
- Modified build logic to detect DNS configuration changes and recreate
the builder container when DNS settings differ

fall back to network gateway

Workflow now adds appropriate exclusions for host-to-container and container-to-container network requests so they aren't all rammed through the proxy.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix

## Motivation and Context
This PR changes the behavior of the Allocation Only vmnet network plugin
to use the default subnet in the fallback case if no subnet was
specified in the network configuration. This matches the behavior of
`ReservedVmnetNetwork`.

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally

- Change behavior of the default arguments in the plugin config (#1063)

## Type of Change
- [x] New feature  
- [x] Breaking change

## Motivation and Context
This PR changes the behavior of the `defaultArguments` field in the
service plugin config. Previously, `defaultArguments` was functioning as
a way to indicate how to start a plugin in the event that the plugin is
loaded at boot (such as for the `container-core-images plugin`).
However, we now follow a convention where all plugins have a "start"
command that is used when launching the plugin, so this
`defaultArguments` field wasn't really providing much. Instead, there
are use cases where we may want to set default values to pass to a
plugin. This PR repurposes the `defaultArguments` field for those use
cases.

As an example use case, there are scenarios where someone may want to
use the AllocationOnlyVmnetNetwork even when running on macOS 26+. This
PR adds the ability to pass in a command line option to the vmnet
network plugin to specify that request. Combined with the
`defaultArguments` plugin config change, a user may choose to set that
field to ["--variant", "allocationOnly"] in the
`container-network-vmnet-config.json` to use AllocationOnlyVmnetNetwork
by default for all networks.

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally

- Throw error when starting a container with invalid virtiofs source (#1051)

Run = Create + Start

1) Mount source points to a valid directory
- Run and Create + Start both correctly create the container with mount.

2) Mount source points to a file
   - Run fails bootstrapping the container, thus container not created.
- Create creates the container, but Start fails bootstrapping, removing
the container. (Thus, both are the same.)

3) Mount source deleted or replaced to file after container created
   - Start throw errors but do not delete the container.

- Fix flaky basic-tool-calling-prompt-test

The test was expecting a strict order of messages, but there's a race
condition between progress messages ("Calling tool", "Generating") and
tool state messages (toolCallRunning, toolCalled). Their relative order
in the middle section is non-deterministic.

Это улучшение упрощает анализ и синхронизацию расшифрованной речи с исходным аудио, обрабатывая и объединяя временные метки на уровне токенов из модели ASR.
updates.source_content:
- Add word-level timestamps support to CLI transcribe command (#193)

## Summary
fixes #189 
This PR adds a new `--word-timestamps` flag that displays timing
information for each word in the transcription output, making it easier
to analyze and synchronize transcribed speech with the original audio.

## Implementation Details

The feature works by:
1. Taking token-level timings from the ASR model output
2. Detecting word boundaries (whitespace characters)
3. Merging consecutive tokens into complete words
4. Averaging confidence scores across tokens that form each word

## Actual CLI Output

```
==================================================
[6:59:58.651 PM] [INFO] [FluidAudio.Transcribe] BATCH TRANSCRIPTION RESULTS
==================================================
[6:59:58.651 PM] [INFO] [FluidAudio.Transcribe] Final transcription:
Hello world!

Word-level timestamps:
  [0] 0.160s - 0.800s: "Hello" (conf: 0.999)
  [1] 0.800s - 1.440s: "world!" (conf: 0.771)

Performance:
  Audio duration: 1.48s
  Processing time: 0.12s
  RTFx: 12.07x
  Confidence: 0.862

[DEBUG] Token timings (count: 5):
  [0] ' H' (id: 425, start: 0.160s, end: 0.480s, conf: 0.998)
  [1] 'ello' (id: 3164, start: 0.480s, end: 0.800s, conf: 1.000)
  [2] ' wor' (id: 2088, start: 0.800s, end: 0.880s, conf: 0.953)
  [3] 'ld' (id: 2493, start: 0.880s, end: 1.360s, conf: 1.000)
  [4] '!' (id: 8020, start: 1.360s, end: 1.440s, conf: 0.362)
```


**Token merging example from output above:**
- ASR tokens: `[" H", "ello", " wor", "ld", "!"]` (5 tokens)
- Merged words: `["Hello", "world!"]` (2 words)
- **"Hello"**: Merged from `" H"` (0.160s-0.480s) + `"ello"`
(0.480s-0.800s) → 0.160s-0.800s
- **"world!"**: Merged from `" wor"` (0.800s-0.880s) + `"ld"`
(0.880s-1.360s) + `"!"` (1.360s-1.440s) → 0.800s-1.440s

- add support for custom vocabulary (#213)

### Why is this change needed?
Custom lexicons exist to let users override pronunciation for
domain-specific terminology that general-purpose G2P and built-in
dictionaries either do not support of mishandle —this is especially
common in finance (tickers, company names, jargon like “EBITDA”),
healthcare (drug names, procedures, acronyms), legal (Latinisms, case
citations), and tech (product names, abbreviations). The goal is for
these overrides to be dependable and to take effect exactly when the
user expects resulting in fluid audio generation.

- feat(diarizer): add speaker count constraints (minSpeakers, maxSpeakers, numSpeakers) (#220)

## Summary

Adds speaker count constraint parameters to
`OfflineDiarizerConfig.Clustering` to fix under-segmentation in
multi-speaker audio scenarios.

Closes #217

## Problem

When processing audio with a known number of speakers (e.g., a 3-speaker
podcast), the diarizer may detect fewer speakers than expected due to
similar voice characteristics or acoustic conditions.

## Solution

Following [pyannote's
approach](https://github.com/pyannote/pyannote-audio/blob/develop/pyannote/audio/pipelines/speaker_diarization.py),
this PR adds:
- `minSpeakers` / `maxSpeakers` - bounded speaker detection
- `numSpeakers` - exact speaker count override
- K-Means re-clustering when VBx violates constraints

## Changes

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `OfflineDiarizerTypes.swift` | Added `minSpeakers`, `maxSpeakers`,
`numSpeakers` to `Clustering` struct |
| `SpeakerCountConstraints.swift` | New helper for resolving and
validating bounds |
| `KMeansClustering.swift` | New K-Means implementation for
re-clustering |
| `VBxClustering.swift` | Added `refineWithConstraints()` method |
| `OfflineDiarizerManager.swift` | Wired up constraint resolution |

## Usage

```swift
// Bounded detection (2-5 speakers)
let config = OfflineDiarizerConfig.default.withSpeakers(min: 2, max: 5)

// Exact speaker count
let config = OfflineDiarizerConfig.default.withSpeakers(exactly: 3)
```

- feat: add partial callback for real-time ghost text (#230)

## Why is this change needed?
I have a use case where I need to show streaming speech to text as it
lands. Currently there's no partials for me to latch onto in the
`StreamingEouAsrManager`. This adds that support; tested and using
successfully on this fork.



https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5c1f1d49-0f10-4a93-8eaa-4d35338a4b0f



## Summary
Add `setPartialCallback()` to `StreamingEouAsrManager` that fires after
each chunk with the current accumulated transcript.

This enables real-time "ghost text" display during speech - useful for
live transcription UIs that want to show text as it's being spoken
before the utterance is finalized.

## Changes
- Add `PartialCallback` type alias (matching existing `EouCallback`
pattern)
- Add `partialCallback` private property
- Add `setPartialCallback(_:)` public method
- Invoke callback after each chunk's token accumulation in
`processChunkAndDecode()`

## Usage
```swift
await manager.setPartialCallback { transcript in
    // Update UI with partial transcript (ghost text)
    print("Partial: \(transcript)")
}
```

The callback receives the full accumulated transcript after each 320ms
chunk is processed, allowing UIs to display evolving text before EOU is
detected.

- feat: Support emitting transcription progress percentage (#229)

Resolve https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio/issues/228

- Fix: Use async prediction API in segmentation prewarm to prevent hang (#227)

## Summary

The synchronous `MLModel.prediction(from:options:)` call in
`prewarmSegmentationModel()` can hang indefinitely on macOS when the
Neural Engine (ANE) is contended after model compilation.

## Problem

When running FluidAudio's offline diarization on macOS, the process
hangs at 0% CPU after the Segmentation model is compiled:

```
[INFO] Compiled model Segmentation.mlmodelc in 334.48 ms
<hangs indefinitely>
```

The root cause is the synchronous prediction call in
`prewarmSegmentationModel()`:
- `MLModel.prediction(from:options:)` blocks until ANE resources are
available
- After model compilation, the ANE may be in a contended state
- No timeout mechanism exists for synchronous prediction
- The process hangs indefinitely waiting for ANE

## Solution

Convert `prewarmSegmentationModel()` to use the async prediction API
introduced in iOS 17 / macOS 14:

```swift
// Before (hangs)
private func prewarmSegmentationModel(_ model: MLModel) throws {
    _ = try model.prediction(from: provider, options: options)
}

// After (yields properly)
private func prewarmSegmentationModel(_ model: MLModel) async throws {
    _ = try await model.prediction(from: provider, options: options)
}
```

Benefits of async prediction:
- Yields while waiting for ANE resources instead of blocking
- Supports task cancellation
- Prevents deadlocks during model initialization
- Thread-safe and integrates with Swift concurrency

## Testing

Tested on:
- macOS 26.1 (Tahoe) with Apple M4 Pro
- The hang was reproducible before the fix
- After the fix, model initialization completes successfully

## References

- [WWDC23: Improve Core ML integration with async
prediction](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2023/10049/)
- [Hugging Face: Async Core ML
inference](https://huggingface.co/docs/swift-transformers/async-inference)

Co-authored-by: Alex <36247722+Alex-Wengg@users.noreply.github.com>

caused the merging to skip some audio because the remainder was not

- Solution: Made it so that 14.96 seconds of audio was collected
i(nstead of 14.99 seconds) to ensure that the start of every chunk is
aligned with the start of every frame.
- Resolve #212

- fix(diarizer): use K-Means centroids when speaker count constraint is applied (#236)

## Summary

Fixes the bug where `numSpeakers` constraint was not being applied to
final diarization result.

**Root cause**: `computeCentroids()` always used `gamma/pi` from VBx
output to compute centroids, ignoring the K-Means centroids stored in
`vbxOutput.centroids` when `wasAdjusted=true`.

**Fix**: Check `wasAdjusted` flag first and use `vbxOutput.centroids`
directly when K-Means was applied due to speaker count constraints.

## Reproduction (before fix)

```swift
let config = OfflineDiarizerConfig.default.withSpeakers(exactly: 2)
let diarizer = OfflineDiarizerManager(config: config)
let result = try await diarizer.process(audioURL)
// Expected: 2 speakers
// Actual: 3 speakers (constraint ignored)
```

`computeCentroids()` when `wasAdjusted=true`

for constraint enforcement

- Mainly used 1 audio clip for testing because only 51.wav (in #232) was

- feat(tts): add SSML tag support for phoneme, sub, and say-as (#235)

### Why is this change needed?
Text-to-speech applications often require fine-grained control over
pronunciation that automatic phoneme generation cannot provide. Names,
acronyms, technical terms, and numbers frequently need explicit
pronunciation guidance or special interpretation rules. This change adds
SSML (Speech Synthesis Markup Language) tag support to Kokoro TTS,
enabling developers to override pronunciations with IPA phonemes via
<phoneme>, substitute text before synthesis with \<sub\>, and control
how content types like dates, numbers, and telephone numbers are spoken
using \<say-as>\. The implementation follows W3C SSML standards and is
designed to co-exist with the existing markdown-style [word](/phonemes/)
phonetic override syntax as well as the [word](replacement) syntax —both
approaches can be used together in the same text, with phonetic
overrides from both sources merged during preprocessing. This gives
developers flexibility to choose whichever annotation style fits their
use case while maintaining full backward compatibility.

- fix: StreamingEouAsrManager.swift: Fix race condition causing crash a… (#247)

StreamingEouAsrManager.swift: Fix race condition causing crash at
removeFirst
The process() method has an await suspension point inside a while loop.
   Between checking audioBuffer.count and calling removeFirst(), another
actor method (like reset()) can clear the buffer, causing removeFirst()
   to crash when it tries to remove more elements than available.

- fix: remove Tokenizer from ParakeetEOU required models (#246)

ModelNames.swift: Remove tokenizer.model from ParakeetEOU.requiredModels
The tokenizer.model file doesn't exist in the HuggingFace repo and isn't
used by StreamingEouAsrManager.loadModels() which uses vocab.json
instead.

- fix: Swift 6 Sendable errors with macOS 26.2 SDK (#245)

### Why is this change needed?
<!-- Explain the motivation for this change. What problem does it solve?
-->

Fixes build failures with Xcode 16 / macOS 26.2 SDK where
AVAudioPCMBuffer
captured in AVAudioConverterInputBlock closures triggers Sendable
errors.

Uses `nonisolated(unsafe)` since the buffers are accessed synchronously
by AVAudioConverter's callback and don't cross actor boundaries.

### Problem
FluidAudio v0.9.0 fails to build with macOS 26.2 SDK (Xcode 16+) due to
strict Swift 6 Sendable checking. The `AVAudioConverterInputBlock`
closure captures `AVAudioPCMBuffer` which isn't marked as Sendable.

### Affected Files
1. `AudioConverter.swift:155-165` - `buffer` captured in input block
2. `StreamingAudioSourceFactory.swift:128-155` - `inputBuffer` captured
in input block

### Errors

```
error: capture of 'buffer' with non-Sendable type 'AVAudioPCMBuffer' in a '@Sendable' closure
error: capture of 'inputBuffer' with non-Sendable type 'AVAudioPCMBuffer' in a '@Sendable' closure
```

- fix: chunk boundary transcription loss due to missing mel context (#264)

## Summary
Fixes transcription truncation at chunk boundaries where valid speech
was being lost.

## Problem
Audio at certain chunk boundaries produced all-blank predictions. The
FastConformer encoder's depthwise convolutions require left context from
preceding audio to produce stable features for the first frames of each
chunk. Without this context, the encoder output for initial frames can
be unstable, causing the TDT decoder to predict silence.

## Solution
Prepend 80ms (1280 samples = 1 encoder frame) of context from the
overlap region to non-first chunks:
- Reserve space in `chunkSamples` calculation to stay within CoreML's
240k sample limit
- Use existing `contextFrameAdjustment` parameter to tell decoder to
skip context frames
- Context is drawn from the existing 2.0s overlap region (no additional
memory)
 
## Testing
- Verified on long-form audio (>2 minutes) that previously exhibited
truncation
- WER improved significantly on affected files
- Streaming mode unaffected (already handles left context correctly)
 
## Notes
This aligns batch mode context handling with how streaming already
works.

- Update README.md (#263)

Added Dictate Anywhere open source project to the Showcase

### Why is this change needed?
Adding my open source macOS dictation app to the showcase. It uses
FluidAudio's Parakeet ASR for on-device speech recognition.

- fix: replace legacy FileHandle.write with throwing write(contentsOf:) (#262)

## Summary
- Replace `FileHandle.write(_:)` with `write(contentsOf:)` to fix
intermittent crashes during diarization
- `FileHandle.write(_:)` is legacy Objective-C API that throws
`NSException` (uncatchable in Swift)
- `write(contentsOf:)` throws Swift `Error` that can be properly caught
- Falls back to stdout via `print()` on failure

#261

- `OfflineEmbeddingExtractor.swift` - emitProfileLog
- `OfflineSegmentationProcessor.swift` - emitProfileLog

Кроме того, улучшена совместимость с API OpenAI для конечной точки /v1/models и устранены критические ошибки сборки Docker. - fix: group sharded model files in auto-discovery (#147) (#157)

* fix: group sharded model files in auto-discovery (#147)

- Add regex-based detection for sharded model patterns (model-XXXXX-of-XXXXX.ext)

This resolves the issue where sharded SafeTensors models were listed as
individual entries instead of being grouped together as a single model.

* style: format code with cargo fmt

* fix: remove unused variable prefixes in AMD GPU detection test

- Fixed compilation error where variables were prefixed with underscore but used without underscore
- This was causing test failures during release gate validation

- Fix #142: AMD GPU detection on Windows (#156)

* Fix #142: AMD GPU detection on Windows

- Add configure_gpu_environment() method to set GGML_* environment variables before backend initialization
- Fix GPU layer assignment by ensuring OpenCL/Vulkan/CUDA backends have proper environment setup
- Add comprehensive regression tests for all GPU backend environment configuration
- Fix compiler warnings with documented #[allow(dead_code)] attributes for conditionally-used MoeConfig fields

Root cause: GPU backends require environment variables set before llama.cpp initialization.
AMD GPUs detected by clinfo but layers assigned to CPU due to missing GGML_OPENCL/GGML_VULKAN variables.

Tests: All 6 release gates pass with zero warnings. Regression tests added for GPU backend validation.

* Fix compiler warnings in issue 142 regression test

- Prefix unused variables with underscores to suppress warnings
- Variables are conditionally used based on feature flags

- Fix OpenAI API compatibility for frontend integration (Issue #113) (#155)

- Remove extra fields (root, parent, permission) from /v1/models response
- Create separate ListModel struct for models endpoint that matches OpenAI spec exactly
- Update created timestamp to use proper system time instead of 0
- Update all tests to use the new ListModel structure

Root cause: Frontend applications like Open WebUI and AnythingLLM expect strict OpenAI API compliance. The extra fields in shimmy's Model struct were causing them to reject the API as incompatible.

Fix ensures /v1/models returns only: id, object, created, owned_by - matching OpenAI specification exactly.

- Fix Docker build failure (Issue #152) (#154)

- Add missing COPY benches/ ./benches/ to Dockerfile
- Update Rust version from 1.75-slim to 1.85-slim for lock file compatibility
- Add libclang-dev and cmake build dependencies
- Add Docker build regression test to release gates

Root cause: Dockerfile was missing benches/ directory copy, causing Cargo manifest parsing to fail. Also missing build dependencies for llama.cpp-sys compilation.

updates.title: Updates in main (5 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Этот выпуск в основном сосредоточен на значительных улучшениях и исправлениях в процессе публикации образов Docker. Он вводит автоматическую публикацию как в GHCR, так и в Docker Hub, гарантируя постоянную доступность версионированных тегов и тега "latest", даже если публикация в `crates.io` завершится неудачей. Кроме того, критическое исправление ошибки решает проблему усечения символов Unicode во время потоковой передачи токенов, предотвращая ошибки декодирования UTF-8 путем соблюдения границ многобайтовых символов.
updates.source_content:
- Release workflow: tolerate Cargo.lock changes; always run Docker publish step (avoid skipped GHCR push)

- Use --allow-dirty for crates.io publish to avoid transient Cargo.lock blocking release

- Added Docker image publishing to GHCR in release workflow

- Fixed Issue #146: Docker image publishing pipeline failures
- Added automated Docker Hub publishing to release workflow

- Fix Issue #139: Unicode character handling in token streaming (#159)

- Fixed stop token truncation to respect UTF-8 character boundaries
- Prevents FromUtf8Error when multi-byte characters are split during truncation
- Added regression tests for Unicode handling in token streaming
- Ensures callbacks receive valid UTF-8 strings

The issue was that stop token removal could truncate strings in the middle
of multi-byte Unicode characters (like emojis), causing UTF-8 decoding errors.
Now we find the proper character boundary before the stop token.

- style: format code with cargo fmt (#158)

updates.summary_ru: Обновление добавляет экспериментальный режим компьютерного зрения для визуальной автоматизации и устраняет проблемы с обнаружением плагинов на торговых площадках. Оно также перерабатывает управление идентификаторами страниц для лучшей совместимости с LLM и включает несколько обновлений зависимостей, в частности для `puppeteer` и `chrome-devtools-frontend`, наряду с общими исправлениями и улучшениями документации.
updates.source_content:
- chore: experimental vision mode (#745) this PR adds the `--experimental-vision` argument that exposes additional tool for visual automation (currently, click_at(x, y)). - fix: use relative path for plugin source in marketplace (#724) The previous GitHub self-reference format was not recognized by Claude Code when adding this repository as an external marketplace. Using a relative path `./` follows the pattern used by other official plugins like [Sentry](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-for-claude/blob/main/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json) and ensures proper plugin discovery. - test: fix flaky network test by normalizing accept-language header (#743) - refactor: change pageIdx to page ids (#741) This allows for order-independent page IDs that are still easy to consume by LLMs (incremental integers). - chore(build): remove obsolete protocol_client.js modifications (#739) The `self.Protocol` assignment and register call have moved to the InspectorBackend constructor. The `self.Protocol` assignment now use `globalThis`. The register call is necessary to make DevTools foundation work. - chore(deps-dev): bump chrome-devtools-frontend from 1.0.1555430 to 1.0.1556696 in the bundled-devtools group (#666) Bumps the bundled-devtools group with 1 update: [chrome-devtools-frontend](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/devtools-frontend). Были добавлены ключевые функции, такие как структурированные сетевые ответы, поддержка `filePath` в инструментах производительности и возможность отказа от аргументов запуска Chrome по умолчанию. Также реализовано исправление для `resize_page` в полноэкранном режиме, обновлена документация и актуализированы зависимости, включая исправление безопасности для `hono`.

- chore: Update eslint rule to require empty line after license notice. (#784) We should make sure there is always an empty line after license notice, otherwise it gets dropped during build if it happens to be before import statement. --------- Co-authored-by: Piotr Paulski - docs: Update README.md to include a link to Android debugging (#783) - docs: add a mention of evals into contributing.md (#773) - chore: refactor eval script more (#781) add args parsing and simplify output (support debug logging + headless). - chore: add more eval scenarios (#780) - docs: update auto-connect docs (#779) Refs https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp/issues/775 - chore: move gemini to agents (#776) - chore: support structured network (#774) This PR adds a structured variant of the network responses and refactors the code accordingly. - chore: implement telemetry persistence and daily active logging (#769) This PR implements the persistence layer for the telemetry system. It introduces `FilePersistence` for local state management and integrates it with `ClearcutLogger` to support "Daily Active" metric. I have decided not to send `first_time_installation` events since we can deduce them from `daily active` events where the `days_since_last_active` will be `-1` for that case. **Implementation Roadmap:** This is the third in a series of PRs designed to implement the telemetry system: 1. **CLI & Opt-out Mechanism ([Merged](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp/pull/757)):** * Added `--usage-statistics` flag and transparency logging. 2. **Logger Scaffolding & Integration ([Merged](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp/pull/758)):** * **`ClearcutLogger`**: Implemented the main logging entry point. * **One-way Data Flow**: Integrated `logToolInvocation` and `logServerStart` hooks into `main.ts` to capture events. * **`ClearcutSender`**: Introduced a transport abstraction. * **Type Definitions**: Added TypeScript definitions for the telemetry Protocol Buffer messages. 3. **Persistence Layer (This PR):** * **`FilePersistence`**: Implemented a local file-based state manager to persist the `lastActive` timestamp. * **Daily Active Logic**: Integrated persistence into `ClearcutLogger` to automatically detect and log `daily_active` events (with `days_since_last_active` calculation) via `logDailyActiveIfNeeded`. 4. **Watchdog Process Architecture (Next):** * Move `ClearcutSender` execution to a dedicated watchdog process to ensure reliable event transmission even during abrupt server shutdowns. 5. **Transport, Batching & Retries (Next):** * Finalize `ClearcutSender` with actual HTTP transport logic, including event batching and exponential backoff retries. - Release notes

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.11.4

Security

Fixed a JWT algorithm confusion issue in the JWT and JWK/JWKS middleware.

Both middlewares now require an explicit algorithm configuration to prevent the verification algorithm from being influenced by untrusted JWT header values.

If you are using the JWT or JWK/JWKS middleware, please update to the latest version as soon as possible.

JWT middleware

import { jwt } from 'hono/jwt'

app.use(
'/auth/*',
jwt({
secret: 'it-is-very-secret',
alg: 'HS256', // required
})
)

JWK/JWKS middleware

import { jwk } from 'hono/jwk'

app.use(
'/auth/*',
jwk({
jwks_uri: 'https://example.com/.well-known/jwks.json',
alg: ['RS256'], // required (asymmetric algorithms only)
})
)

For more details, see the Security Advisory.

updates.title: Updates in main (29 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Этот выпуск добавляет новые возможности эмуляции устройств (область просмотра, пользовательский агент) и значительно улучшает управление снимками, позволяя опциональную генерацию для инструментов ввода и повторное использование идентификаторов узлов в Chrome DevTools MCP. Отладка улучшена благодаря включению трассировки стека с сопоставлением исходного кода в сообщениях консоли и усовершенствованным структурированным выводам для консольных и производительных инструментов. Релиз также включает инструменты для управления расширениями, внедряет надежную систему телеметрии с помощью сторожевого процесса, а также содержит различные обновления зависимостей и исправления ошибок для общей стабильности.
updates.source_content:
- feat: allow skipping snapshot generation for input tools (#821) Input tools have snapshots not re-generated by default now with an option to opt-in to get a snapshot. Refs: https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp/issues/726 - chore: implement bucketized latency reporting for tool invocations (#822) - chore: token count tool (#820) small helper - fix: re-use node ids across snapshots (#814) previously, Chrome DevTools MCP was strictly requiring the client to use the latest snapshot. This change updates the behavior to be more lenient. Previously issued uids will be recognized if the underlying backend Id (loaderId + backendNodeId) still exists. updates.summary_ru: Это изменение исправляет нарушение правила одного определения (ODR) для функций `cpp/raw` во время AOT-компиляции. Проблема возникала из-за многократной обработки идентичных вызовов. Решение реализует защиту `#ifndef/#define`, чтобы гарантировать, что вызовы `cpp/raw` с одинаковым строковым содержимым считаются эквивалентными и выполняются только один раз.
updates.source_content:
- Fix ODR violation for cpp/raw functions during AOT compilation (#591)

Fixes #582 .

We use a simple #ifndef/#define guard, so all calls to `cpp/raw` that
have exactly the same content (same string) will be considered
equivalent and run only once.

updates.title: Updates in main (4 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Это обновление значительно улучшает стабильность сборки и выполнения Jank на macOS, особенно в средах nix-darwin. Оно устраняет конфликты между стандартными библиотеками Clang, предоставляемыми ОС и локально собранными, а также улучшает AOT/JIT компиляцию за счет динамической обработки флагов компоновщика и фильтрации путей SDK для обеспечения переносимости. Кроме того, включены улучшения в синтаксический анализ ключевых слов и обработку ошибок.
updates.source_content:
- Clean up and document macOS stdinc fix (#603)

- Add clang args that fix the potential for OS and local Clang build std libs conflicting with each other. (#602)

* Add clang args that fix the potential for OS and local Clang build std libs conflicting with each other.

* Use the new flags conditionally on mac-like platforms.

- Make jank build portable on macOS in nix-darwin environments (#585)

This commit addresses build and runtime issues when jank is compiled on macOS
within a nix-darwin environment, making jank installable via Homebrew on macOS
even when nix-darwin is present.

## Problem

When building in nix-darwin, the SDKROOT and other environment variables are
set to point to nix-managed SDK paths. Although jank builds cleanly on vanilla
macOS, these nix-darwin settings interfere with the build process in two ways:

1. AOT Compilation: Platform-specific linker library requirements need proper
   handling. On macOS, Clang uses libc++ by default and doesn't require explicit
   -lstdc++ linking, while Linux requires it.

2. JIT Compilation: Clang extracts system include paths containing absolute SDK
   paths (e.g., /Applications/Xcode.app/.../MacOSX.sdk/usr/include or
   /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX*.sdk/usr/include). These
   paths get embedded in JANK_JIT_FLAGS and cause header ordering issues at
   runtime when jank performs JIT compilation.

## Solution

### Part 1: Platform-aware AOT compilation with runtime checks
- Moved -lstdc++ linking decision from build-time CMake to runtime C++ code
- Use if constexpr(jtl::current_platform != jtl::platform::macos_like) checks
- This approach is simpler and more maintainable than CMake configuration files
- On macOS: Exclude -lstdc++ (uses libc++ implicitly via Clang)
- On Linux: Include -lstdc++ (requires explicit linking)
- Removed -L/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/lib/unwind which is not needed on macOS

### Part 2: Filter SDK paths from JIT compilation flags
- Create a filtered version of clang_system_include_flags for JIT compilation
- Exclude paths matching /SDKs/ from JIT flags while preserving them for
  the build itself

This separation ensures:
- Build-time includes: Use unfiltered paths (need SDK headers for compilation)
- JIT runtime flags: Use filtered paths (SDK comes from -isysroot at JIT time)

The filtering prevents baking absolute SDK paths into the binary while still
allowing the build itself to find necessary system headers. At JIT time, the
correct SDK is obtained from -isysroot dynamically rather than hardcoded
build-time paths, making jank portable across different macOS/Nix configurations.

## Verification
- Builds successfully with SDKROOT set (nix-darwin environment)
- Builds successfully on vanilla macOS
- JIT compilation works correctly with filtered flags
- All check-health tests pass
- AOT compilation generates correct platform-specific binaries

updates.title: Updates in main (4 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Это обновление включает обновление локфайлов до последней ночной версии (26.1.0.dev2025111705). В `mojo-lang` было удалено избыточное хранение типов из `SugarAttr`, а вывод ключевого синтаксического «сахара» был улучшен для более наглядного объяснения несоответствий типов, при этом поле 'original' в `SugarAttr` было переименовано в 'expanded'. Кроме того, в стандартной библиотеке 'alias' был переименован в 'comptime'.
updates.source_content:
- Update lockfiles to point to latest nightly version: 26.1.0.dev2025111705

- [mojo-lang] Remove stored type from SugarAttr. NFC

This is always available from an operand, so we have no need to
redundantly store it.

MODULAR_ORIG_COMMIT_REV_ID: 098a7803798afdfffa26f001ee99d212b277da19

- [mojo-lang] Always print key sugar even if not explaining. (#72440)

If sugar is a key nested value in a type mismatch, make sure to
unpack it, even if not "diffing". This allows us to print the
expansion of `ideal_width` in the b example.

This also renames "original" to "expanded" in SugarAttr which
makes it easier to explain.

updates.title: Updates in main (56 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Это обновление включает компактный синтаксис MLIR для `SugarAttr` в Mojo, что может экспоненциально уменьшить размер промежуточного представления (IR), а также исправляет ранжирование разрешения перегрузок. Добавлена поддержка FP64 TensorCore для GPU NVIDIA и улучшены возможности параллелизма данных (DP) и распределенного вывода (DI) в TransferEngine и KVCache. Были выполнены обширные внутренние рефакторинги, включая переименование `alias` в `comptime` и миграцию API указателей, а также внесены оптимизации для моделей и средств тестирования. Недавняя интеграция LLVM была отменена из-за регрессии производительности, требующей дальнейшего решения.
updates.source_content:
- Update lockfiles to point to latest nightly version: 26.1.0.dev2025112405

- [mojo-lang] Improve MLIR syntax of SugarAttr for X.y references (#72910)

This introduces a new compact syntactic form for field references.
This can exponentially reduce the size of IR in some cases because
it only prints the type once instead of twice.

- [DI] Support DI with DP

The main changes are tracking replica_idx in scheduler. When performing
a KVCache Transfer between Prefill -> Decode, we need to specify the
src and dst replica_idx. This should theoretically work even if the
Prefill
and Decode have different DP degrees.

- [TransferEngine] Support DP in transfer engine

Now the transfer engine supports both DP and TP.
This is needed for *D*P *D*eepseek with *D*I (The Triple-*D*).

The main difference now is that we specify the src and dst replica
indices
when we begin a transfer. Notice that the src and dst replicas can
differ.
```
// before
transfer_engine.initiate_send_transfer(
    remote_metadata=remote_metadata,
    src_idxs=src_idxs,
    dst_idxs=dst_idxs,
)

// after
transfer_engine.initiate_send_transfer(
    remote_metadata=remote_metadata,
    src_idxs=src_idxs,
    dst_idxs=dst_idxs,
    src_replica_idx=src_replica_idx,
    dst_replica_idx=dst_replica_idx,
)
```

Like how we already support TP, we use different NixlAgent per gpu for
DP.

There is no change needed at the NIXL layer. All the changes are purely
at
the Python transfer engine layer to support `list[list[Tensor]]` instead
of just `list[Tensor]`.

Although transfer engine supports DP + TP at same time, the rest of the
stack does not support them in combination yet fyi.

In a followup PR I will test that DP Llama works.

- [DI] Simplify DI env vars and delete default destination address.

The env vars needed to configure DI are way too convoluted. I am
simplifying them here.

Sample old env var:
```
MAX_SERVE_DISPATCHER_CONFIG='{"transport": "dynamic_zmq", "transport_config": {"bind_address": "tcp://10.0.0.207:7000", "default_destination_address": "tcp://10.0.0.229:6000"}}'
```

This is annoying since it is a json string and we need to take care due
to double quotes and spaces.
You can easily mispecify this due to string escaping woes.

Additionally, it allows us to configure the transport type
("dynamic_zmq") when there are no other options.

Finally, it allows us to pass the "default_destination_address". This
refers to the default prefill node
to forward a request by a decode node if the target endpoint is not
specified for the request. This field
is meaningless for prefill nodes since they do not forward requests. I
am deleting this field and making it
a hard error if target endpoint is not specified for a request.

Now the new env var is much simpler:
```
MAX_SERVE_DI_BIND_ADDRESS=tcp://10.0.0.207:7000
```

This is a simple string that is easy to specify and read.

---

I am on privileged Gcore 2x8xH100 with Infiniband. This is two nodes
with 8 GPUs each.

Here is how to run deepseek with DI. We do not use multi-node EP here.

We use the `kathywu95/deepseek-v3-small-random` version since full
deepseek
does not fit on one 8xh100 node.

MODULAR_DEVICE_CONTEXT_BUFFER_CACHE_SIZE_PERCENT=95 is specified to
leave room
for nvshmem which allocates memory via cuMemCreate. If I set 99, I get a
crash
during inititalization.

prefill-chunk-size=128 is specified to minimize the amount of memory
that
nvshmem allocates.

---

Before:
```
// launch on decode node
MODULAR_DEVICE_CONTEXT_BUFFER_CACHE_SIZE_PERCENT=95 \
  MAX_SERVE_SCHEDULER_STATS_LOG_INTERVAL_S=0 \
  UCX_TLS="rc,ud,dc,cuda_copy,cuda_ipc" \

- [MAX] Don't divide batch size by Data Parallelism degree

When you specify --data-parallel-degree 8 --max-batch-size 32 there are
two ways to interpret this:
1. Each of the 8 DP replicas has a cap on batch size of 32. Across all
replicas the aggregate max batch size is thus 8 * 32 = 256.
2. Each of the 8 DP replicas has a cap on batch size of 4. Across all
replicas the aggregate max batch size is thus 32.

Currently our code uses interpretation #2. However, I think we should
switch to #1 for the following reasons:
- Maintaining max_batch_size and max_batch_size_per_replica is very
error prone. It is very easy to mix them up.
- This interpretation is consistent to what vLLM does.

- [mojo-lang] Struct extensions naming/importing changes, attempt 2 (#72954)

Re-merges the compiler parts of
[Internal link] which were always fine
but caught up in the revert of the stdlib changes.

This PR does three main changes:

* Cleanup: Makes extensions (eg extension MyStruct) known to their
parents not as their struct's name ("MyStruct") but instead prefixed
with "extension:" ("extension:MyStruct"). This makes it so
lookupAndResolveDecl("MyStruct") doesn't return the extensions as well.
This is good because we generally like finding and resolving as little
as possible.
* Makes extensions (eg extension MyStruct) also known to their parents
as "extension:". This is helpful when we want to look up "all extensions
in a given scope", which is useful for the next point.
* Makes it so when we import anything from a module, we also import all
extensions (we just look for anything named "extension:").

Note that this might not be the final design, this makes an assumption
that if a file wants to use an extension, then that extension is in a
file that is indirectly imported. It's similar to Rust/Swift/C#/Kotlin,
but we might want to be more similar to Python, which just makes all
extensions globally visible to everyone everywhere, despite all the
spooky action at a distance that entails (doc incoming on this).

This PR adds a quantization kernel for FP4 Activations. It follows the

simillar to flashInfer we

- [mojo-lang] Struct extensions naming/importing changes (#72612)

Re-merges the compiler parts of
[Internal link] which were always fine
but caught up in the revert of the stdlib changes.

This PR does three main changes:

* Cleanup: Makes extensions (eg extension MyStruct) known to their
parents not as their struct's name ("MyStruct") but instead prefixed
with "extension:" ("extension:MyStruct"). This makes it so
lookupAndResolveDecl("MyStruct") doesn't return the extensions as well.
This is good because we generally like finding and resolving as little
as possible.
* Makes extensions (eg extension MyStruct) also known to their parents
as "extension:". This is helpful when we want to look up "all extensions
in a given scope", which is useful for the next point.
* Makes it so when we import anything from a module, we also import all
extensions (we just look for anything named "extension:").

Note that this might not be the final design, this makes an assumption
that if a file wants to use an extension, then that extension is in a
file that is indirectly imported. It's similar to Rust/Swift/C#/Kotlin,
but we might want to be more similar to Python, which just makes all
extensions globally visible to everyone everywhere, despite all the
spooky action at a distance that entails (doc incoming on this).

- [stdlib] Simplify SIMD dunder relational methods

This commit simplifies several SIMD dunder relational methods.

The methods work by calling into their respective non-dunder variants,
which return SIMD bool vectors. Those are then used to create a `Bool`
using the constructor and the `ImplicitlyBoolable` trait, which calls
back into SIMD's `__bool__` method.

Instead, we can avoid this roundtrip by calling `__bool__` ourselves.
This keeps things in the SIMD domain and avoids the trait interface.

An added benefit of this is that this specific `Bool` constructor is not
supported by `@always_inline("builtin")` due to an unsupported argument
convention. Future work will thus be able to mark these dunder
relational methods `@always_inline("builtin")` and enable better support
for SIMD types in `where` clauses.

This teaches Mojo to infer generic error types to `Never` when presented with a function that doesn't raise. This completes the core support for "parametric raises" by subsuming the Swift "rethrows" extension. For example, given a generic map function: ```mojo # This simple "map" function is generic over closure throwability. fn int_list_map[ ErrorType: AnyType ]( mut list: List[Int], fp: fn (arg: Int) raises ErrorType -> Int ) raises ErrorType: for ref elt in list: elt = fp(elt) # Example function that raises. fn partial_function(arg: Int) raises -> Int: if arg > 100: raise Error("Argument too large") return arg * 2 # Example function that does not raise. fn complete_function(arg: Int) -> Int: return arg + 1 # Usage examples fn examples(mut list: List[Int]): # This can throw so it needs to be in a try block. try: int_list_map(list, partial_function) except err: print(err) # This can't throw so it doesn't need to be in a try block. int_list_map(list, complete_function) ``` MODULAR_ORIG_COMMIT_REV_ID: 2adf059f3f7ab3be41c439bf46c537fe5d1b50cd - [stdlib] polish: Remove ambiguous `String.join` variadic overload (Part 2.5/N) This avoids a change in overload resolution behavior that will occur when making `List` conform to `Writable`. Code such as `"foo".join([1, 2, 3])` ought to resolve to the `String.join(Span)` overload, but could theoretically also resolve to this removed variadic overload as a single-element variadic argument pack. That does not occur today because the variadic overload requires the elements to implement `Writable`, which `List` does not _today_. updates.title: Updates in main (61 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Это обновление включает обширный рефакторинг в ядре (kernels) и стандартной библиотеке, в частности, перенос многочисленных тестов ядра и кода матричного умножения для ЦП с `HostNDBuffer` на другие механизмы. Стандартная библиотека Mojo получила значительные улучшения, в том числе изменения в неявных преобразованиях, введение эффекта `extern` и доработки вариативных типов и инициализации списков. Кроме того, реализованы оптимизации производительности в конвейерах для таких моделей, как Qwen, улучшения в планировщике, а также различные обновления документации и исправления в системе сборки, включая включение Mypy в репозиторий с открытым исходным кодом.

- [stdlib] polish: Use `T: ConvertibleToPython` in args instead of `PythonObject` (Part 2/N)

As part of aiming at removing the `@implicit` decorator from
`PythonObject` initializers, but to preserve the ability to do things like:

    var obj = PythonObject(5)

    var res = obj * 5

it is necessary that e.g. `PythonObject.__mul__` change from taking the
RHS as a `PythonObject`, and instead take a `T: ConvertibleToPython`.

From a callers perspective, this is largely the same: you can pass
simple values like `5` and it gets converted to a `PythonObject` either way.

But making the conversion be part of `__mul__` instead of a general
feature of `PythonObject` means that such implicit conversions can be avoided in
cases where they would be surprising.

NOTE: This has some known caveats / issues of it's own, but we believe
those are less-bad than leaving the current `@implicit` decorators as they are.

Known issues include:

* This technically will enable _more_ types to be "implicitly" converted
to PythonObject
* This makes these functions generic, potentially increasing code size
and compile times.
(These functions like likely commonly be stamped out with multiple
different input parameter types)

MODULAR_ORIG_COMMIT_REV_ID: e2d93cc543ee16fdaffddc79950c157aafdefdcd

- [stdlib] Migrate a few `is_integral` checks to where clauses

This commit migrates some uses of `__comptime_assert
dtype.is_integral()` to `where dtype.is_integral()` clauses on function
signatures. This provides better type safety by enabling compile-time
constraint checking.

The remaining 22 `is_integral` uses cannot be migrated due to a compiler
limitation: the constraint propagation system cannot prove constraints
when:

1. **Call sites lack constraint evidence**: Functions are called from
contexts where the compiler cannot prove the dtype is integral (e.g.,
from `builtin/simd.mojo`, `io/write.mojo`)

2. **Calling non-always-inline-builtin functions**: Functions use DTypes
returned from compile-time functions like `get_accum_type[dtype]()`, and
the compiler cannot evaluate non-builtin functions to infer their return
type properties

3. **Transitive constraint dependencies**: Functions call other
functions that require constraints, creating chains where evidence
cannot propagate through multiple levels

We explored using `@always_inline("builtin")` as a workaround for
constraint propagation, but this annotation is too restrictive:

- Does not support `@parameter if` statements
- Does not support `__comptime_assert`
- Does not support some `llvm_intrinsic` patterns
- Even with `where` clauses, call sites still cannot prove constraints

- [LoRA] Fix a bug with the sequence boundary between the K and V
extension of the input-row-offsets

Fix a bug introduced with the LoRA KV optimizations. Instead of using
the end of the LoRA sequences for the KV offsets boundary, I foolishly
used the end of the whole sequence as the boundary. For example, lets
say we have 4 requests and 2 use LoRA. If our `total_seq_len = 256` and
our `lora_seq_len = 128`, then prior to this fix, we would create a
tensor of size `total_seq_len * 2` and our `lora_grouped_offsets = [0,
64, 128, 320, 384]`. Our first group in V would span 192 tokens which is
completely incorrect. The KV computation needs to know where the LoRA
sequences end and also needs a properly sized tensor to support this
computation correctly. The correct tensor of size is `lora_seq_len * 2`
and our offsets should be `lora_grouped_offsets=[0,64,128 192, 256]`.
Now group 0 in V is correctly 64 tokens instead of 128.

- Update lockfiles to point to latest nightly version: 26.1.0.dev2025121217

- [Kernels] Support asymmetric padding in `conv` kernels

This PR updates our `Conv1D`/`Conv2D`/`Conv3D` APIs to accept a tuple
in the case of asymmetric padding. Because the underlying cuDNN kernel
does not accept asymmetric padding, we pre-pad the inputs manually in
`conv.mojo:conv_gpu` and invoke the existing kernels with zero padding.
Integration tests are also added for both the FCRS (`permute=True`) and
non-FCRS paths to validate correctness.

- [Scheduler] Cap max_batch_size if it is larger than prefill_chunk_size

These is needed for Deepseek. Deepseek triggers a weird edge case in DP
scheduler
when max_batch_size is larger than prefill_chunk_size. This is because
currently
max_batch_size=512 and prefill_chunk_size=128. The prefill_chunk_size is
low
since the model is still under development. All other models use a
larger
value for prefill_chunk_size so this edge case never materializes.

The bug manifests in the following way:
- Replica 1: TG w/ 512 reqs with 512 inputs tokens for 10 steps
- Replica 2: CE w/ 1 req with 128 inputs tokens for 1 step

Then we merge these two batches into a mega batch:
- Replica 1, 2: CE w/ 513 reqs and 640 inputs tokens for 1 step

The "merge" just takes the min num_steps from each replica. And if any
replica batch is CE, then the mega batch is CE.

Clearly this mega CE batch is illegal since 640 input tokens >
prefill_chunk_size * dp

To avoid this, we just make it illegal to have max_batch_size larger
than prefill_chunk_size

On a aside, it may be worthwhile to rename `prefill_chunk_size` to
`max_num_batched_tokens` since the value
now imposes a limitation of TG as well. `max_num_batched_tokens` is used
by vLLM et al.
At the very least `target_tokens_per_batch_ce` needs to be renamed to be
consistent
with pipeline config.

- [KVCache] Massive refactor of KVCache graph construction

This PR simply moves `.get_symbolic_inputs()` from `kv_manager` to
`kv_params`.
This allows one to construct the graph purely with `kv_params` without
needing
the whole manager. The whole manager comes with a ton of baggage like
needing
a realized `Device` (not just a `DeviceRef`) and allocating a whole
bunch
of KVCache memory.

This PR works towards getting rid of the NullKVCacheManager. The
NullKVCacheManager
essentially allows for graph construction via `.get_symbolic_inputs()`
but
does not allocate memory. In a later PR, we will just simply use kv
cache
params for graph construction instead.

This shift of more responsibility to the `kv_params` means that the
params
need `devices : list[DeviceRef]` instead of just `n_devices : int`. This
required a TON of plumbing for each model to achieve. Future PRs will
follow
up and clean up the plumbing.

One ugly thing is that now we pass the kv_cache_params `list[DeviceRef]`
to the constructor of KVCacheManager as well as a `list[Device]`. This
is
redundant! I think we should just have the following in the future:

```
kv_manager = params.build_manager()
```

- [LlamaVision] Delete MultimodalKVCache and support Llama Vision by
juggling 2 KVCache managers

The prev multimodal KVCache manager was a bit of a hack. It juggled 2
KVCache managers in a single object.

This design makes it extremely annoying to make changes to the KVCache
manager.

Each time we changed the KVCache manager, we had to change the
multimodal KVCache manager.
Plus Llama Vision kept breaking for random reasons.

This PR refactors Llama Vision to use 2 separate KVCache managers. This
refactor is subtle but will make it less likely to break in the future.

Now I am no longer motivated to delete Llama Vision.

Added a new docstring to warn folks about tech debt:
```
This is a hybrid model that combines full attention with cross attention.
To support this, we utilize two KVCache managers: one for the text model and
one for the vision model.

The text KVCache follows the standard pattern used all across our stack. However,
the vision KVCache is a bit of a hack. Each page is sized to fit up to the max
vision sequence length and each request is always allocated exactly one page.

Our implementation of this is a bit questionable as our support for hybrid
models is still nascent. For instance, in many parts of our stack we assume
that we only have a single KVCache manager.

As such, there be dragons here. Tread carefully.
```

- [stdlib] feat: Enable linear types in `UnsafePointer`, `VariadicPack`, and other fundamental APIs (Part 7/N)

A 'linear type' or 'non-implicitly-destructible' type is a type without
a `__del__` method, that may only be destroyed by calling a named
`deinit self` method.

This means that linear types have even fewer restrictions than today's
`AnyType`, which requires that a type at least have `__del__`.

Many "core" operations like `size_of` or `rebind` don't actually depend
on a type having an implicit destructor, so they can be updated to instead require
the `UnknownDestructible` trait, which truly does have no requirements.

This PR demonstrates that linear types are compatible with the
primitive building blocks of Mojo, including `VariadicPack` (and the variadics
helpers), `UnsafePointer`, and `Pointer`.
