Множественные исправления также направлены на устранение сбоев CI/CD, проблем сборки и нестабильности тестов на различных платформах и языках, повышая общую надежность и совместимость проекта.
updates.source_content:
- fix: resolve CI failures across Ruby, Homebrew, and WASM

- fix(ruby): use keyword argument for path in E2E helper
  Change extract_file_sync call to use `path:` keyword argument
  instead of positional argument to match API signature

- fix(homebrew): move download_with_retry function before first usage
  Function was defined after being called, causing "command not found"
  error during bottle downloads

- fix(wasm): use URL-based path resolution for Windows compatibility
  Use `new URL()` with import.meta.url for cross-platform module
  resolution instead of relative string paths that fail on Windows

- fix(ci): add Windows tessdata setup for Elixir CI

Add Tesseract tessdata download step for Windows in Elixir CI workflow.
Downloads eng.traineddata and osd.traineddata to C:/tess/tessdata and
sets TESSDATA_PREFIX environment variable.

This fixes Tesseract-related test failures on Windows where tessdata
files were not available.

- fix(ruby): handle unknown config keys in from_file and discover

The Rust FFI config_from_file returns all keys from the config file,
but the Ruby Extraction.initialize only accepts specific keys. This
caused CI failures when extra keys (like 'images') were present.

This fix:
- Adds ALLOWED_KEYS constant defining valid config keys
- Adds KEY_ALIASES for backward compatibility (images -> image_extraction)
- Filters out unknown keys before passing to initialize
- Applies to both from_file and discover methods

Fixes Ruby CI test failures for config_spec.rb:194,203,212,222,231,
241,250,259,269,276,296,410 and extraction_config_spec.rb:295,303.

- fix(pptx): resolve extraction failures for shapes without txBody and add PPSX/PPTM support

Fixes GitHub Issue #321:

Bug 1 - "No txBody found" error:
- PPTX extraction now gracefully skips shapes without txBody (e.g., image placeholders)
- Changed parse_sp() to return Option<ParsedContent> instead of failing

Bug 2 - PPSX files not supported:
- Added .ppsx extension to MIME type mapping (slideshow format)
- Added .pptm extension to MIME type mapping (macro-enabled format)
- Both MIME types added to SUPPORTED_MIME_TYPES set

Also includes:
- 4 regression tests covering both bugs
- PPSX sample file for testing
- Version bump to 4.1.1 with changelog entry

- fix: CI failures and crates.io publishing

- Restore kreuzberg-tesseract version constraint for crates.io publishing
- Skip Windows tests for PHP and Go CI (Tesseract installation issues)
- Fix Ruby test fixtures: rename 'images' to 'image_extraction'

- ci(node): temporarily disable Windows TypeScript tests

E2E tests hang indefinitely on Windows. Build job still runs to

- fix(sync): Update jsonl_file_hash in finalizeExport to prevent spurious warnings (#1113)

The JSONL file hash mismatch warning was appearing consistently after
git commit operations, even when no actual data inconsistency existed.

Root Cause:
Two code paths export to JSONL but only one updated jsonl_file_hash:
- flushToJSONLWithState() (used by bd update/create): Updated both
  jsonl_content_hash AND jsonl_file_hash
- finalizeExport() (used by bd sync --flush-only): Updated only
  jsonl_content_hash, NOT jsonl_file_hash

Since validateJSONLIntegrity() checks jsonl_file_hash, any bd command
after a git commit would see a mismatch and trigger the warning.

Steps to Reproduce (before fix):
1. cd /path/to/beads-project
2. bd update -p 3 some-issue-id  # Works fine, stores hash H1
3. git add .beads/issues.jsonl && git commit --amend --no-edit
   # Pre-commit hook runs bd sync --flush-only
   # This updates jsonl_content_hash to H2 but leaves jsonl_file_hash as H1
4. bd update -p 3 some-issue-id  # WARNING appears!
   # validateJSONLIntegrity() compares file (H2) with jsonl_file_hash (H1)
5. Repeat steps 3-4 indefinitely - warning always appears

The fix adds SetJSONLFileHash() call to finalizeExport(), ensuring both
export paths update the same metadata consistently.

updates.source_content:
- feat(show): add --id flag for IDs that look like flags

When an issue ID starts with dashes (e.g., gt--kzx), it can be
misinterpreted by Cobra's argument parser. The new --id flag allows
these IDs to be passed safely:

  bd show --id=gt--xyz

Multiple --id flags can be used, and they can be combined with
positional arguments.

Closes: bd-ix0ak

Adds bd doctor --server to diagnose Dolt server mode connections:
- Server reachability (TCP connect to host:port)
- Dolt version check (verifies it is Dolt, not vanilla MySQL)
- Database exists and is accessible
- Schema compatible (can query beads tables)
- Connection pool health metrics

Supports --json for machine-readable output.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

- fix(dolt): server mode should support multi-process access

Code review fix: In server mode, Dolt connects to an external sql-server
and should NOT be single-process-only. The whole point of server mode is
to enable multi-writer access.

Changes:
- Add Config.GetCapabilities() method that considers server mode
- Update daemon_guard, daemon_autostart, daemons, main to use GetCapabilities()
- Add TestGetCapabilities test
- Update init command help text to document server mode flags

The existing CapabilitiesForBackend(string) is kept for backward compatibility

- fix(sqlite): use BEGIN IMMEDIATE without retry loop (GH#1272)

The original PR added retry logic on top of BEGIN IMMEDIATE, but this caused
multi-minute hangs because:

1. Connection has busy_timeout=30s set via pragma
2. Each BEGIN IMMEDIATE waits up to 30s before returning SQLITE_BUSY
3. With 5 retries, worst case was 5 × 30s = 150+ seconds

The fix removes the retry loop since SQLite's busy_timeout already handles
retries internally. BEGIN IMMEDIATE still acquires the write lock early,
preventing deadlocks - we just let busy_timeout handle contention.

Root cause analysis in bd-9ldm.

* feat(mol): add 'bd mol seed --patrol' command

Adds `bd mol seed` command to verify formula accessibility before
patrols attempt to spawn work.

## Problem

Gas Town's `gt rig add` calls `bd mol seed --patrol` but this command
didn't exist in beads, causing the call to always fail and fall back
to creating non-functional placeholder beads.

## Solution

Implemented `bd mol seed` with two modes:

1. **With --patrol flag**: Verifies all three patrol formulas are accessible
   - mol-deacon-patrol
   - mol-witness-patrol
   - mol-refinery-patrol

2. **Without --patrol**: Verifies a specific formula is accessible

## Implementation

The command uses `resolveAndCookFormulaWithVars` to verify formulas:
- Checks formula search paths (.beads/formulas/, ~/.beads/formulas/, $GT_ROOT/.beads/formulas/)
- Validates formula syntax and resolution
- Confirms formula can be cooked to subgraph

## Usage

```bash
bd mol seed --patrol                    # Verify all patrol formulas
bd mol seed mol-feature                 # Verify specific formula
bd mol seed mol-review --var name=test  # With variable substitution
```

## Testing

- ✅ Command compiles without errors
- ✅ Help text displays correctly
- ✅ `--patrol` succeeds when formulas accessible (town level)
- ✅ `--patrol` fails with clear error when formulas missing (rig level)
- ✅ Follows existing beads command patterns (cobra, flags, error handling)

## Impact

- Enables Gas Town's intended patrol formula verification flow
- Eliminates creation of unnecessary placeholder beads
- Provides health check command for formula accessibility
- Foundation for future seed commands (data initialization, etc.)

Fixes the missing command referenced in steveyegge/gastown#715

- Eliminated duplication between daemon and direct modes

Add type filtering support to `bd linear sync --push` to allow users to

- fix(routing): close original store before replacing with target store (#1215)

* fix(routing): close original store before replacing with target store

Fix "database is closed" error during auto-flush when contributor routing
redirects issue creation to a different repository (e.g., ~/.beads-planning).

When a user is detected as a contributor (based on git remote URL pattern),
the default configuration routes new issues to ~/.beads-planning instead of
the current repository. This routing caused auto-flush to fail with:

  Warning: auto-flush failed: failed to get stored JSONL hash:
  failed to get jsonl_file_hash: sql: database is closed

In create.go, when switching to the planning repo:
1. targetStore was opened for the planning database
2. A defer was set to close targetStore at function end
3. store = targetStore replaced the global store pointer
4. Issue was created successfully
5. Command Run ended → defer closed targetStore
6. PersistentPostRun tried to flush using the global store → error!

The bug: the defer closed targetStore, but the global `store` variable
pointed to the same object. When PersistentPostRun called flushManager.Shutdown(),
it tried to use the already-closed store for the flush operation.

- Remove the defer that prematurely closed targetStore
- Explicitly close the ORIGINAL store before replacing it (it won't be used)
- Let PersistentPostRun close whatever store is current at exit time

This ensures proper store lifecycle:
- Original store: closed when replaced (no longer needed)
- Target store: closed by PersistentPostRun after flush completes

1. Have a git repo with a remote URL that doesn't match maintainer patterns
   (e.g., github-a:org/repo.git instead of git@github.com:org/repo.git)
2. Have ~/.beads-planning directory with beads initialized
3. Run: cd /path/to/repo && bd create "Test issue"
4. Observe: Issue created successfully, but followed by:
   Warning: auto-flush failed: ... sql: database is closed

Added debug prints to SQLiteStorage.Close() and GetJSONLFileHash() which
revealed two different databases were involved:
- /path/to/repo/.beads/beads.db (closed first, unexpectedly)
- ~/.beads-planning/.beads/beads.db (used for flush after being closed)

* fix(test): resolve race condition in TestAutoFlushOnExit

Not directly related to the previous routing fix, but exposed by CI timing.

Root cause: The test had a latent race condition between two channel operations:
1. markDirtyAndScheduleFlush() sends event to markDirtyCh
2. Shutdown() sends request to shutdownCh

Without any delay, Go's scheduler might process the shutdown event first.
Since isDirty was still false (markDirty event not yet processed), the
FlushManager would skip the flush entirely, causing the test to fail with
"Expected JSONL file to be created on exit".

The race was always present but only manifested in CI environments with
different timing characteristics (CPU contention, virtualization, scheduler
behavior).

Fix: Add a 10ms sleep after markDirtyAndScheduleFlush() to allow the
FlushManager's background goroutine to process the event before shutdown.
This mimics real-world behavior where there's always some time between
CRUD operations and process exit.

- fix(routing): disable auto-routing by default (#1177)

Change routing.mode default from "auto" to "" (empty/disabled).

This fixes GH#1165 where fresh `bd init --prefix X` followed by
`bd create` would unexpectedly route to ~/.beads-planning and fail
with "database not initialized: issue_prefix config is missing".

Auto-routing now requires explicit opt-in via:
- `bd init --contributor` flag, OR
- `bd config set routing.mode auto`

Includes test verifying the default and doc updates clarifying
the opt-in requirement.

- fix(types): show custom types when daemon is running (#1216)

The `bd types` command only checked `if store != nil` to fetch custom
types. In daemon mode, `store` is nil (daemonClient handles RPC instead),
so custom types were never displayed even when configured.

This caused a mismatch where `bd config get types.custom` showed the
correct values but `bd types` showed none.

Fix by calling ensureDirectMode() at the start of the command, matching
the pattern used by `bd config get`. This falls back from daemon mode
to direct storage access when needed.

- /{cmd,internal}: fix lint issues

- /{website,internal,docs,cmd}: integration tests and more split backend fixes

- /{cmd,internal}: get dolt backend init working and allow issue creation

- fix(tui): Log and discard drained pending ExecCells (#214)

### Motivation

- Pending ExecCells that were "drained" at the end of a prompt were
being appended into the chat transcript and could appear after long
assistant summaries, confusing the conversation flow.
- Instead of inserting these stale cells into history, we should log
detailed diagnostics (with timestamps) at warning level and discard them
so transcripts remain sane.

### Description

- Introduce a `PendingCellEntry` (with `initial_pending_at` and
`last_update_at`) and change `cells` to `HashMap<String,
PendingCellEntry>` in
`codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/pending_exec_cells.rs`.
- Update `save_pending()` to record/update timestamps and preserve
multi-call mappings.
- Change `drain_failed()` to log a detailed `tracing::warn!` per pending
cell (call ids, pending call ids, counts, initial/last/drain timestamps
and durations) and discard the cells, returning the discarded count
instead of returning cells for insertion into history.
- Update `retrieve()` to unwrap `PendingCellEntry` to the inner cell as
before.
- Stop inserting drained pending cells into history by removing the
insertion loop in `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget.rs` so drained cells are
no longer added to the transcript.
- Update documentation (`docs.md` and `EXEC_CELL_LIFECYCLE.md`) to
reflect the new drain semantics and adjusted test expectations.

### Testing

- Ran formatting with `just fmt` in `codex-rs`, which completed
successfully.

operations to be invisible in the TUI.

This PR synthesizes ToolCall SessionUpdate events when these methods are
invoked, enabling the TUI to render file operations from Gemini agents
just like it does for Claude.

-  now emits ToolCall event before reading files
-  now emits ToolCall event before writing files

## Technical Details

The implementation:
1. Extracts the  from the client capability request
2. Creates a synthetic with descriptive title (e.g., "Reading
path/to/file") and status
3. Sends it through the session's update channel (same mechanism as real
session updates)
4. The existing translator picks this up and renders it in the TUI

- Tests verify event structure (title, kind, status)
- All existing tests continue to pass

includes:

content)

- fix(cargo): Make sccache optional to fix release CI/CD builds (#186)

## Summary

- Removed mandatory `rustc-wrapper = "sccache"` from
`codex-rs/.cargo/config.toml`
- Updated documentation to explain optional sccache usage via
`RUSTC_WRAPPER` env var
- Fixes nori-release.yml test job failure without adding complexity to
the release workflow

## Problem

The nori-release.yml workflow's test job failed with:
```
error: could not execute process 'sccache ... -vV' (never executed)
Caused by: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

Root cause: Commit 7cbd16f5c added `rustc-wrapper = "sccache"` to the
cargo config, making sccache mandatory for all builds. However, the
release workflow doesn't install sccache.

## Solution

Instead of adding sccache to the release CI/CD (which adds complexity),
this PR makes sccache optional:

- Removed the `rustc-wrapper` line from cargo config
- Developers who want sccache benefits (disk savings across worktrees)
can enable it via:
  ```bash
  export RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache
  ```
- The rust-ci.yml workflow already uses this env var approach (line
105), so CI performance is unaffected
- Keeps the release workflow simple and transparent

## Test plan

variable
- [x] Updated documentation in codex-rs/docs.md
- [ ] CI/CD tests will verify the fix works in the release workflow

## Related

- Fixes the failure seen in
https://github.com/tilework-tech/nori-cli/actions/runs/20931911438/job/60147855852
- Alternative to commit c877c14c5 which added sccache to the release
workflow

detection and per-user opt-out control.
- Send telemetry to the Nori analytics proxy using a flat event schema
and non-blocking delivery with strict timeout requirements.

### Description

- Replace prior user-id with a deterministic `client_id` UUID derived
from `SHA256("nori_salt:<hostname>:<username>")` and add an `opt_out`
boolean to the install state file schema.

`app_update`, `user_resurrected`, `session_start`), detect semver
upgrades via the `semver` crate, and flag resurrection when last launch
> 30 days.
- Revamp analytics payload to a flat JSON shape (`event`, `client_id`,
`session_id`, `timestamp`, `properties`) and post to
`NORI_ANALYTICS_URL` (default
`https://noriskillsets.dev/api/analytics/track`) with a 500ms timeout
and fire-and-forget semantics.
- Honor opt-out precedence with `NORI_NO_ANALYTICS=1` overriding local
`opt_out`, keep state updates even when opted out, and document the new
schema and behavior in `docs.md`.
- Add dependencies (`semver`, `uuid`) and update tests and code to use
the new API names (`generate_client_id`, `create_event`, etc.).

## Summary

- Implement conversation compaction for ACP backend using a prompt-based
approach
- When user invokes `/compact`, send summarization prompt to agent,
capture response, and prepend to next user message
- Enable token reduction in long conversations while working within
ACP's stateless architecture

## Implementation Details

The ACP backend cannot directly access conversation history like the
core backend, so we use a prompt-based approach:

1. Send `SUMMARIZATION_PROMPT` (from `codex_core::compact`) to the agent
2. Capture the agent's text response as the summary
3. Store summary in `pending_compact_summary:
Arc<Mutex<Option<String>>>`
4. On next user input, prepend the summary using `SUMMARY_PREFIX`

Includes:
- Proper idle timer handling (cancel at start, restart on completion)
- Error handling with partial summary cleanup on failure
- `ContextCompactedEvent` and `WarningEvent` emission for TUI
notification

updates.summary_ru: Это обновление представляет новую утилиту для динамического построения и выполнения графовых моделей ONNX во время выполнения, использующую ONNX Runtime Model Editor API. Она обеспечивает гибкое и эффективное выполнение на различных аппаратных платформах, позволяя динамически создавать и кэшировать операции, а также интегрирована с провайдером выполнения WebGPU. Эти изменения значительно повышают гибкость и удобство поддержки графовых операций во время выполнения, приводя к приросту производительности, например, к увеличению на 12% для моделей phi4 на NV 5080.
updates.source_content: - Implement graph models for EPs (#1895) This pull request introduces a new graph model building and execution utility using the ONNX Runtime Model Editor API, and integrates it with the WebGPU execution provider. The changes enable dynamic creation and caching of ONNX models (such as Cast and TopK operations) at runtime, allowing for flexible and efficient execution across different hardware backends. The most important changes are grouped below: **Graph Model Building and Execution Utilities:** * Added new files `graph_builder.h` and `graph_builder.cpp` implementing the `ModelConfig`, `TensorConfig`, and `AttributeValue` types, and a `GraphBuilder::Build` function to construct ONNX models dynamically using the Model Editor API. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ab0bfe9d45e482a78a9dff68d1ad90a00c60ec90190dac3a701d2a9343698079R1-R80) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-54c386bc82f44fa10113920e8e0613be6a967efa5d0e731e15014540639013f8R1-R226) * Added new files `graph_executor.h` and `graph_executor.cpp` providing `GraphExecutor::Execute` and a helper `ExecuteCastOp`, enabling execution of dynamically built models with session caching keyed by model configuration and execution provider. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-09edfaf45433f0a3a49cbe3b1d4bfbddd65f98b006085267d05947143cd50203R1-R70) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0fe7b88593c1d2c3f7ca19a20d41f8bfed5c7b0eff302a29760e47584fc16b4aR1-R194) * Updated `onnxruntime_api.h` to expose the Model Editor API via `GetModelEditorApi()`. * Added a session cache to `OrtGlobals` for dynamically built graph sessions, with thread safety via a mutex. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-bc6c7ee0bb3d69f59e0764be50ce24a471e3f415b9110b25a8a5a02a42be4c04R141-R148) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bc6c7ee0bb3d69f59e0764be50ce24a471e3f415b9110b25a8a5a02a42be4c04R16) **WebGPU Integration:** * Updated `src/webgpu/interface.cpp` to use the new graph execution utilities, implementing `InterfaceImpl::Cast` using `ExecuteCastOp` with WebGPU-specific session configuration. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-570e78875f2d5b7e18ea9342f8c172e74392a6f584c1588d910c672d3a225fc7R7) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-570e78875f2d5b7e18ea9342f8c172e74392a6f584c1588d910c672d3a225fc7R180-R209) These changes significantly improve the flexibility and maintainability of runtime graph operations, making it easier to support new ONNX operators and execution providers. With this change, phi4 with graph capture becomes 130.4 tps from 116.2 tps on NV 5080. - fix: patch `llguidance` to remove reference to `ring` crate (#1948) Fix MVS-2022-374v-6mvc by purging references to `ring` from `Cargo.lock`. - Add custom model path support for unit tests (#1917) Add support for custom model paths in unit tests via command-line argument - Added `--model_path` argument to `unit_tests.exe` to specify custom model locations - Updated `test/main.cpp` to parse the custom model path argument - Updated `test/model_tests.cpp`, `test/sampling_benchmark.cpp`, and `test/sampling_tests.cpp` to use custom paths for NvTensorRT tests - Allows running tests with models in non-default locations - Revert "Add a doc showing how to run GPT OSS 20B with WebGPU" (#1950) ### Description This PR reverts the [GPT-OSS 20B WebGPU documentation PR](https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime-genai/pull/1945). ### Motivation and Context The [model and its corresponding documentation](https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime-genai/pull/1945#discussion_r2695919071) are already in the [Hugging Face repo](https://huggingface.co/onnxruntime/gpt-oss-20b-onnx). - Fix QMoE blockwise quantization support for TRT-RTX execution provider (#1926) Add QMoE and BF16 support for TRT-RTX execution provider - Enable blockwise quantization for TRT-RTX/NvTensorRtRtx EPs - Add gpt_oss_swiglu_fusion option for separate gate/up weights - Add int4_qdq_block_size for MatMul quantization block size - Add BF16 precision support for TRT-RTX - Keep padding in QMoE weights for proper alignment - Fix GatherBlockQuantized node to support symmetric quantized LM_HEAD (#1951) Today models created with python -m onnxruntime_genai.models.builder -p int4 -e webgpu --extra_options shared_embeddings=true int4_algo_config=rtn_last int4_is_symmetric=true have invalid GatherBlockQuanntized nodes because the zero point attribute of the node points to a non-existent tensor lm_head.MatMul.weight_zp. This change fixes builder.py, so that we are selective about adding that attribute to the GatherBlockQuantized node. - Add C#, Java, and Objective-C APIs for Config (#1946) ### Description This PR adds the `Config.Overlay` API to C# and Java. It also introduces the `Config` class and its main APIs to Objective-C. ### Motivation and Context This PR aims to bring parity so that the APIs used in the examples are available in all language bindings. It is needed for [this PR](https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime-genai/pull/1939) as well. - Add a doc showing how to run GPT OSS 20B with WebGPU (#1945) - Only manually load DLLs if onnxruntime.dll is not already loaded. (#1800) ## Why is this change made Before this change, when using Windows ML. If the user initialize Windows ML before loading genai, there will be two onnxruntime.dll loaded into the python process, like this: This is because Windows ML will try to load the onnxruntime.dll packed in the Windows App Runtime when it is initialized. But genai will also try to load the dml and ort DLLs packed in the onnxruntime python package. Result in duplicating DLLs. Since Windows ML is not loading the DLL by path, it won't load the its DLL if genai is loaded first. ## What changed This PR checks if onnxruntime.dll is already loaded before loading the dml and ort DLLs manually. After this change, when running a dml model with Windows ML initialized first, the process' loaded library looks like this: When loading WinML after genai, it behaves the same as before. (IMHO, using the DLLs from the Windows App Runtime and dropping the dependency on onnxruntime-winml seems more streamlined.)

updates.title: Updates in main (54 commits)
updates.summary_ru:
This update introduces significant improvements to the `tmux-cli` and `voice` plugins. The `tmux-cli` now offers enhanced reliability for the Enter key, including verification and retry logic, and a new `execute()` method to accurately capture command output and exit codes, even for verbose or historical output. The `voice` plugin's stop hook has been transformed from a blocking mechanism into an auto-summarizing feature that generates concise, tone-matching summaries of the last assistant message using streaming audio, alongside better interrupt handling and overall robustness for hooks.

***

Это обновление вносит значительные улучшения в плагины `tmux-cli` и `voice`. Плагин `tmux-cli` теперь обеспечивает повышенную надежность нажатия клавиши Enter, включая верификацию и логику повторных попыток, а также новый метод `execute()` для точного захвата вывода команд и кодов завершения, даже для подробного или прокрученного вывода. Стоп-хук плагина `voice` был преобразован из блокирующего механизма в функцию автоматического суммирования, которая генерирует краткие, соответствующие тону сообщения, сводки последнего сообщения помощника с использованием потокового аудио, наряду с улучшенной обработкой прерываний и общей надежностью хуков.
updates.source_content:
- chore: bump all plugins to v1.8.4 and update changelog

- fix(hooks): add defensive bash wrapper to prevent blocking on missing files

If the Python hook file doesn't exist for any reason, approve instead
of blocking everything. Applies to both aichat and voice plugins.

- bump: version 1.8.3 → 1.8.4

- Merge branch 'fix/improve-voice-prompt'

- Merge branch 'claude/review-issue-13-TZD1J'

- fix(tmux-cli): capture pane state after text, before Enter for verification

Fixes bug identified by Codex reviewer in PR #46: the verification was
capturing pane content BEFORE sending text, but shells echo input as
it's typed. This meant pane content always changed after sending text
(regardless of Enter), so the retry logic never triggered.

Now captures the baseline AFTER text is sent but BEFORE Enter, so we
properly detect whether Enter caused additional changes (new prompt,
command output, etc).

- Merge pull request #46 from pchalasani/claude/review-issue-13-TZD1J

fix(tmux-cli): improve Enter key reliability with verification and retry

- refactor(voice): simplify stop hook prompt to intuitive framing

Replace 7 prescriptive guidelines with simpler approach:
"You are the assistant who just wrote that message. Give a brief
SPOKEN voice update..." - lets the model use natural judgment

- fix(tmux-cli): improve Enter key reliability with verification and retry

Addresses issue #13 where Enter key sometimes fails to register.

Changes:
- Increase default delay_enter from 1.0s to 1.5s for better reliability
- Add Enter key verification: checks if pane content changed after Enter
- Add automatic retry logic (up to 3 attempts with exponential backoff)
- Add README warning about plain tmux unreliability
- Add directive for users to instruct AI agents to use tmux-cli over tmux
- Update docs to reflect new 1.5s delay and verification behavior

The root cause was that plain `tmux send-keys` sends text and Enter
simultaneously, causing race conditions. tmux-cli now:
1. Sends text first, waits 1.5s
2. Sends Enter and verifies pane content changed
3. Retries Enter if verification fails

Fixes #13

https://claude.ai/code/session_01PU4EGd7sASmY2QnggTGkBC

- fix(voice): add TTS-friendly guideline to avoid technical identifiers

- docs(tmux-cli): document execute as CLI command, not just Python API

- Add execute section to plugins/tmux-cli/README.md
- Fix docs/tmux-cli-instructions.md to show CLI usage first
- The execute subcommand was always available but incorrectly documented

- fix(voice): handle error/non-text messages gracefully in summaries

- fix(voice): enforce 1-2 sentence limit on voice summaries

- fix(voice): restore tone-matching guideline in stop hook prompt

Add guideline #5: match user's tone and colorful language

- chore: bump all plugins to v1.8.3 and update changelog

- Update version to 1.8.3 in all plugin.json files
- Add changelog entry for voice and aichat plugin improvements

- bump: version 1.8.2 → 1.8.3

- Merge pull request #45 from pchalasani/fix/voice-stop-hook-noblock

feat(voice): auto-summarizing stop hook + fix(aichat): defensive guardrails

- fix(voice): improve stop hook prompt to avoid meta-narration

- Restructure prompt with clear demarcation: past conversation (for tone)
  vs last assistant message (to summarize)
- Add guideline to avoid meta-commentary ("I explained", "I gave you")
- Summary should state content directly, not narrate about delivering it
- Remove --model haiku flag to use default model (Opus)
- Use JSON output format for cleaner parsing

- fix(aichat): add defensive coding guardrails to UserPromptSubmit hook

- Wrap entire main() in try/except to fail silently on any error
- Add strict type checking for prompt (must be non-empty string)
- Make pattern matching stricter: exact match OR followed by space
  (prevents false triggers like ">resuming" matching ">resume")
- Lowercase prompt before comparison for case-insensitivity

- Revert "fix(aichat): add matcher to UserPromptSubmit hook to prevent false triggers"

This reverts commit ade51da7f691fb3f2e94130cb633c84943e8a009.

- fix(aichat): add matcher to UserPromptSubmit hook to prevent false triggers

- Add union matcher ">resume*|>continue*|>handoff*|>session*" to hooks.json
- Hook now only runs on specific trigger patterns instead of every prompt
- Simplify Python code since matcher guarantees valid triggers

- fix(voice): improve Haiku summarization with conversation context

- Pass last 5 conversation turns to Haiku (not just last assistant msg)
- Haiku can now pick up on user's tone/colorful language
- Trim assistant messages to 500 words to keep context manageable
- Skip CLAUDE.md files with --setting-sources "" for faster/cleaner calls
- Use first person in summaries ("I did X" not "The assistant did X")

- feat(voice): replace blocking stop hook with auto-summarizing Haiku approach

Instead of blocking and showing "Stop hook error", the new Python hook:
- Reads last assistant message from session JSONL file
- Calls headless Claude Haiku to generate 1-2 sentence summary
- Displays summary via systemMessage field (shows as "Stop says:")
- Runs TTS in background for concurrent text+audio feedback
- Always approves (no blocking, no jarring error display)

This eliminates the disruptive "Stop hook error:" prefix while still
providing voice feedback on task completion.

- docs: updated local LLM set up for glm-4.7-flash

- bump: aichat-search v0.3.0

- bump: version 1.8.1 → 1.8.2

- Merge pull request #44 from pchalasani/fix/rust-tui-debounce

fix(rust-tui): debounce search + fix(voice): correct config path

- fix(voice): correct config file path and remove dead hook

- Change speak command to use voice.local.md (matches what hook reads)
- Change default voice from azure to azelma
- Delete unused user_prompt_hook.sh file

- refactor(rust-tui): simplify event loop, keep debouncing

Revert the event loop restructuring that added unnecessary complexity.
The debouncing alone is sufficient - no need for:
- has_events conditional wrapper
- Multiple terminal.draw() calls
- Processing events before periodic checks

Keep: debouncing + cached column widths (the useful changes)

- fix(rust-tui): debounce search to fix typing lag

- Add debouncing to on_char() and on_backspace() - filter() now runs
  after 200ms of no typing instead of on every keystroke
- Restructure event loop to process events before slow operations
- Cache column widths in filter() instead of recalculating every frame

The core fix is debouncing; other changes are optimizations that may
be reverted if they add unnecessary complexity.

- feat(voice): add tone-matching instruction to voice summaries

Tell agent to match user's communication style in voice feedback.
Added to both SKILL.md guidelines and stop hook message.

- bump: all plugins to version 1.8.1

Sync plugin versions with main package version for consistency.
Updated: aichat, langroid, safety-hooks, tmux-cli, voice, workflow

- bump: version 1.8.0 → 1.8.1

- feat(voice): improve interrupt handling with state tracking

Replace 30-second cooldown with smarter state detection:
- Track -running (with PID), -done, and -failed states
- User interrupts (dead PID, no done/failed) → re-prompt immediately
- TTS failures → approve and don't retry broken server
- Short 5-second grace period only for agent to call say

This ensures user interrupts trigger immediate re-prompting instead of
silently disabling voice feedback for 30 seconds.

- refactor(voice): simplify hook by moving session tracking into say script

- Remove PostToolUse hook that externally tracked say invocations
- Add --session flag to say script, which creates -done flag on completion
- Add robust PID-based locking to prevent hangs after interrupted playback
- Stop hook now passes session ID directly in the say command

This simplifies the architecture: instead of a separate hook watching
for say calls, the say script handles session tracking directly.

- docs: update tmux-cli skill to incl execute

- docs: plugin changelog

- bump: version 1.7.0 → 1.8.0

- Merge pull request #43 from pchalasani/claude/review-issue-42-oNsCX

feat(tmux): Add execute() method for exit code extraction

- fix(tmux): Fix marker parsing to find echoed output, not typed command

The parse_marked_output function was finding markers in the typed command
text rather than the echoed output, causing garbage in the output field.

Changes:
- Search for start marker after newline (\n{marker}) to find echoed version
- Use regex to find end marker with numeric exit code (not $?)
- Add execute() documentation to tmux-cli-instructions.md

Fixes issue where output contained wrapped command text instead of just
the command's actual output.

- Merge branch 'main' into claude/review-issue-42-oNsCX

- fix(voice): queue audio playback with mkdir lock to prevent overlapping voices

- refactor(tmux): Extract polling logic into shared helper function

Eliminates ~30 lines of duplicated code between TmuxCLIController and
RemoteTmuxController by moving the progressive expansion polling loop
into poll_for_completion() in tmux_execution_helpers.py.

Each controller's execute() method is now ~25 lines instead of ~50.

Refs: #42

- feat(tmux): Add progressive expansion to execute() for verbose commands

Addresses Codex Review Agent feedback on PR #43 (Issue #42).

The previous implementation captured only 100 lines, causing false
timeouts when commands produced verbose output (start marker would
scroll off screen). Now progressively expands capture:
100 → 500 → 2000 → unlimited lines.

Changes:
- Add find_markers_in_output() helper to tmux_execution_helpers.py
- Update execute() in both TmuxCLIController and RemoteTmuxController
- Add 6 tests for the new helper function

Refs: #42

- docs(voice): update changelog with streaming and cooldown fixes

- fix(voice): add 30-second cooldown to stop hook to prevent API error loops

When Claude Code encounters API errors (especially with thinking blocks),
the retry mechanism can cause the stop hook to block repeatedly, creating
an infinite loop. This fix checks the block flag's timestamp and auto-approves
if we blocked within the last 30 seconds, breaking the retry loop while still
allowing fresh blocks on new conversation turns.

- feat(voice): add streaming audio playback for lower latency

- Use ffplay to pipe TTS output directly when FFmpeg is available
- Fall back to temp file approach (afplay/aplay) without FFmpeg
- Update READMEs to recommend FFmpeg installation
- Add troubleshooting section for slow audio playback

- docs: add plugins changelog

- fix(voice): prevent infinite loop in stop hook by tracking block attempts

- docs: Add reverse-pagination optimization note for scrollback capture

- docs: Update proposal with branch link and scrollback discovery

- Fix: Capture more history lines in execute() to handle scrollback

When panes have scrollback history, markers can scroll off the visible
screen before capture. Now capturing last 100 lines to ensure markers
are included in captured output.

Fixes timeout issue where exit_code=-1 was returned even though
commands completed successfully.

- Implement exit code extraction with execute() method

Add execute() method to capture command exit codes using unique markers:

New files:
- claude_code_tools/tmux_execution_helpers.py: Helper functions for marker
  generation, command wrapping, and output parsing
- tests/test_tmux_execution_helpers.py: Unit tests for helper functions

Modified files:
- claude_code_tools/tmux_cli_controller.py: Add execute() to TmuxCLIController
  and CLI class
- claude_code_tools/tmux_remote_controller.py: Add execute() to RemoteTmuxController
- tests/test_tmux_cli_controller.py: Add tests for execute() method

Implementation details:
- Uses echo markers (START/END) to wrap commands and capture exit codes
- Returns structured JSON: {output: str, exit_code: int}
- 30-second default timeout, configurable per-call
- exit_code=-1 on timeout
- Works in both local (pane) and remote (window) modes

Tested with TDD approach - all tests pass.

- Add proposal for exit code extraction feature

Proposes adding execute() method to capture command exit codes via markers.
This enables reliable error handling for LLM-driven tmux automation.

Based on battle-tested patterns from personal sane-* toolkit developed
through friction-analysis of LLM failures in production environments.
